I admire them because the experience showed me what good research can look like. I'm studying AI and robotics myself, so I find this kind of example especially relevant. The place felt noisy because several different sounds were happening at the same time. It was harder to concentrate than it would have been in a quiet room. I would occasionally look at the display again to make sure I hadn't missed anything important.

I don't think the noise was completely avoidable, because a station is a busy public place. Still, clear announcements and a quieter waiting area would make it more comfortable. We talked about everyday things rather than trying to discuss serious work the whole time. I mentioned some anime I'd been interested in, and we also shared stories about things that had happened recently. The conversation moved naturally from one topic to another.

After dinner, we took a short walk instead of leaving immediately. There wasn't a particular attraction we needed to see. We just continued chatting and enjoyed having time together without a deadline.

I learned by applying the method to a real task and explaining each step during our discussion. Instead of giving me the answer immediately, they asked questions that helped me see what evidence I had and what I was only assuming.

questions.title: 有健康习惯和作息的人
questions.text:
Describe a person you know who has healthy habits and a healthy daily routine
You should say:
Who this person is
How you got to know each other
What he/she does to keep this lifestyle
And explain how you feel about him/her
questions.english:
A person I know with healthy habits is a friend from university. We got to know each other through classes and shared study activities, and their routine stood out because it was steady rather than extreme.

They try to go to bed at a reasonable time and avoid leaving every task until late at night. During the day, they take short breaks from the computer and go for a walk when possible. They also prepare simple meals instead of depending on snacks whenever they are busy.

What I find sensible is that they don't treat health as a competition. If a deadline makes one day difficult, they return to their normal habits afterwards rather than give up completely. They plan ahead, but still leave room for meeting friends or enjoying a relaxing evening.

I respect that approach because studying can make it easy to spend a long time sitting and forget basic needs. Their routine shows that looking after yourself doesn't require a complicated system. Small actions repeated over time can be more realistic than a dramatic change that lasts only a few days. I'd like to learn from that consistency.
questions.chinese:
我认识的一位有健康习惯的人，是大学里的一位朋友。我们通过课程和一起学习认识，对方的作息让我印象深刻，因为这些习惯很稳定，并不是靠极端做法维持的。

这位朋友尽量在合理的时间睡觉，避免把所有任务都拖到深夜。白天会短暂离开电脑休息一下，有机会就出去散步。即使忙碌，也会准备简单的饭菜，而不是总靠零食解决吃饭的问题。

我觉得很合理的一点是，对方不把健康当作一场比赛。如果某天因为赶任务而难以保持作息，之后就恢复平时的习惯，而不是彻底放弃。对方会提前安排事情，但仍然给见朋友或度过一个轻松的晚上留出空间。

我很欣赏这种做法，因为学习时很容易长时间坐着，忘记自己的基本需要。这套作息说明，照顾好自己并不需要复杂的系统。长期坚持的小行动，可能比只持续几天的大幅改变更现实。我想学习的正是这种持续性。

questions.title: 读起来开心的书
questions.text:
Describe a book you enjoyed reading and that made you happy
You should say:
What kind of book it was
What it was about
Why you read it
And explain why it made you happy
questions.english:
A book I enjoyed reading is The Little Prince. It is a short imaginative story that looks simple at first, but raises questions about friendship, responsibility, and how adults see the world.

The story follows a young prince who leaves his small home and visits different places. Along the way, he meets characters whose lives are shaped by things such as power or numbers. His relationships with a rose and a fox give the story a more personal and emotional side.

I chose it because I wanted something different from technical reading. As an AI student, I spend time thinking about systems and practical problems, so a gentle story offered a change of pace. I could read a little without feeling that I had to memorize every detail.

It made me happy because it encouraged me to pay attention to simple relationships rather than only measurable achievements. I also liked the contrast between the child's questions and the adults' complicated habits. The book didn't solve a particular problem, but it left me calmer and reminded me that curiosity and care are valuable. That's the kind of feeling I want from leisure reading.
questions.chinese:
我喜欢读的一本书是《小王子》。这是一部充满想象力的短篇故事，乍看很简单，却提出了关于友谊、责任以及成年人如何看待世界的问题。

故事围绕一位离开自己小小家园、前往不同地方的年轻王子展开。一路上，他遇见了生活被权力、数字等事物主导的人物。他与玫瑰和狐狸之间的关系，也让故事更有个人情感色彩。

我选择这本书，是因为想读一些与技术材料不同的内容。作为人工智能专业的学生，我会花时间思考系统和实际问题，因此这样一个温和的故事能让我换一种节奏。我可以读上一小段，而不用觉得自己必须记住每一个细节。

它让我开心，因为它鼓励我关注简单的人际关系，而不只是可以衡量的成就。我也喜欢孩子的提问与成年人复杂习惯之间的对比。这本书没有解决某个具体问题，但它让我更平静，也提醒我好奇心和关怀很有价值。这正是我希望从休闲阅读中获得的感受。

questions.title: 帮助他人
questions.text:
Describe a time when you helped someone
You should say：
Where you helped him/her
Why you helped
How you helped
And explain how you felt about it
questions.english:
A time I helped someone was when a classmate was struggling with a small programming task at university. We were in a study area, and they had a program that seemed to run but didn't produce the expected result.

I offered to help because I knew how frustrating that situation could be. At first, I didn't change the code. I asked them to explain what they wanted it to do and what they had already checked. Then we reduced the task to a simpler example and looked at the output step by step.

Eventually, we noticed that one part of the program was using the wrong input. After fixing that, we tested it again and checked that the result matched the goal. I also explained why the smaller example had made the problem easier to locate.

I felt pleased, mainly because my classmate could continue independently afterwards. I enjoy programming, but helping someone understand a process is different from solving everything for them. It was a fairly ordinary event, yet it showed how useful patient questions can be. I also learned to explain my own thinking more clearly instead of assuming that the other person saw the problem in the same way.
questions.chinese:
我帮助别人的一次经历，是大学里一位同学做小型编程任务时遇到了困难。当时我们在一个学习区，对方的程序似乎可以运行，却没有产生预期的结果。

我主动提出帮忙，因为我知道这种情况会有多令人沮丧。一开始，我没有改代码，而是请对方解释希望程序完成什么，以及已经检查过哪些地方。然后，我们把任务简化成一个更小的例子，一步步查看输出结果。

最后，我们发现程序中的一个部分使用了错误的输入。修正后，我们重新测试，确认结果符合目标。我也解释了为什么这个更小的例子能让问题更容易定位。

我感到很高兴，主要是因为之后同学可以独立继续做下去。我喜欢编程，但帮助别人理解一个过程，与替对方解决所有问题是不同的。虽然这是一次很普通的经历，却让我看到耐心提问有多有用。我也学会了更清楚地解释自己的思路，而不是假定别人看待问题的方式与我相同。

What it is about
Why you watched it
And explain how you feel about it
questions.english:
An interesting video I watched showed a robot handling everyday objects. I watched it on my computer at home one evening when I wanted a short break from studying.

The robot had to identify items and place them in the right positions. The video didn't only show a perfect final result. It also included an attempt that went wrong and showed how the system tried again. That made it more interesting than a simple display of fast, impressive movements.

I watched it because my master's studies focus on AI and robotics. I wanted to see an example of a robot dealing with the physical world, where objects can move and small errors matter. Something that looks easy for a person can involve several difficult problems for a machine.

I felt curious and motivated afterwards. The most useful part was thinking about the gap between a successful demonstration and a reliable system people could use every day. I didn't regard the video as proof that the problem had been completely solved. Instead, it gave me a clear example to think about and reminded me why practical robotics remains such an interesting research area.
questions.chinese:
我看过的一个有趣视频，展示了一台机器人如何处理日常物品。某天晚上，我想在学习之余短暂休息一下，就在家里的电脑上看了这个视频。

机器人需要识别物品，再把它们放到正确的位置。视频并不只展示一个完美的最终结果，也包括了一次失败的尝试，以及系统如何重新尝试。相比单纯展示快速、令人惊艳的动作，这样的内容让我觉得更有趣。

我会看这个视频，是因为我的硕士学习重点是人工智能和机器人。我想看看机器人应对物理世界的例子：在这个世界里，物品会移动，细小的误差也很重要。一个对人来说看似简单的动作，对机器来说可能涉及好几个难题。

看完之后，我感到好奇，也更有动力。最有价值的是思考成功演示与人们能够日常使用的可靠系统之间还有什么差距。我没有把这个视频当作问题已经完全解决的证明，而是把它看作一个清晰、值得思考的例子。它也提醒我，为什么实用机器人仍然是如此有趣的研究领域。

questions.english: A video often spreads when it creates a strong reaction, such as surprise, amusement, or recognition. A clear idea that people understand quickly is easier to share. Timing and platform recommendations can help too. However, attention is unpredictable, and a viral video isn't necessarily accurate or valuable. I think shareability explains popularity better than simply having expensive production.
questions.chinese: 视频带来惊讶、好笑或认同等强反应时常传播。易快速理解的清晰想法更易分享。时机和平台推荐也有用。但注意难预测，爆款不一定准确有价值。我认为易分享比昂贵制作更能解释流行。

questions.title: 去过的无聊地方
questions.text:
Describe a boring place
You should say:
Where it is
Who you went there with
What you did there
And explain why you think it is a boring place
questions.english:
A place I found boring was a large furniture showroom in the city where I live. I went there with my mother one afternoon because we wanted to look at some options for the home.

At first, I was interested in the different room designs. But after a while, many displays began to feel similar. We walked between rows of sofas, tables, and cupboards, checked labels, and discussed small differences in size and colour.

The visit took longer than I had expected because there were many choices and it was difficult to narrow them down. I could see why those details mattered, but I didn't feel very involved in the process. There wasn't much to do except keep looking and comparing.

I think the place was boring for me because the activity didn't connect strongly with my interests. I enjoy reading and programming, where I can follow an idea or solve a problem. In the showroom, the decisions felt repetitive and I had no clear task of my own. I wouldn't say it was a bad place; it was useful for its purpose. I would simply prefer a shorter visit with a clearer plan.
questions.chinese:
我觉得无聊的一个地方，是我现在居住的城市里的一家大型家具展厅。某天下午，我和母亲一起去了那里，因为我们想看看有哪些适合家里的选择。

起初，我对不同的房间设计还有兴趣，但过了一会儿，很多展示开始让我觉得大同小异。我们在一排排沙发、桌子和柜子之间走动，查看标签，讨论尺寸和颜色上的细小差别。

这次逛展厅比我预期的时间更长，因为选择很多，很难缩小范围。我理解为什么那些细节很重要，但自己并没有很强的参与感。除了继续看、继续比较，也没有多少其他事情可做。

我觉得这个地方无聊，是因为这项活动与我的兴趣联系不大。我喜欢阅读和编程，因为可以顺着一个想法深入，或者解决一个问题。但在展厅里，做决定显得很重复，我自己也没有明确的任务。我不会说那里不好，它确实满足了自己的用途。我只是更希望参观时间短一些，事先的计划更明确一些。
pending: 家具购物、陪母亲、时间地点、具体行为和感受均为授权候选；母亲同住与兴趣为真，不扩写真实家装事实。

questions.title: 去过的无聊地方
questions.text: Why do most children think education is boring?
questions.english: Lessons can feel boring when children only listen, memorize, and repeat information without seeing its purpose. Work that is too easy or too difficult can also reduce interest. Practical activities and meaningful questions may help students become more involved. I think the problem is often how learning is presented, rather than children having no curiosity about the world.
questions.chinese: 孩子只听、背、复述信息而看不到目的时，课可能无聊。太容易或太难的任务也降低兴趣。实践活动和有意义问题帮助参与。我认为问题常在呈现学习的方式，而非孩子对世界无好奇。

questions.title: 去过的无聊地方
questions.text: Why aren’t young people willing to listen to the experiences of older people?
questions.english: Young people may feel that older people's experiences don't match the world they live in, especially when technology or work has changed. Advice can also sound like criticism if it isn't invited. However, practical wisdom may still be relevant. Older people can explain without lecturing, and younger people can ask questions before deciding whether an experience offers something useful.
questions.chinese: 年轻人可能觉得老人的经历与当下世界不符，尤其技术工作改变时。未经请求的建议也可能像批评。但实际智慧仍相关。老人可解释而非训话，年轻人可先提问，再判断经历是否有用。

questions.title: 去过的无聊地方
questions.text: What can people do when they feel bored?
questions.english: People can change what they are doing rather than keep scrolling on their phones. A short walk, a conversation or a small practical task can make a difference. Sometimes boredom also means an activity feels pointless, so choosing something with a clear goal, like learning a skill, may help more than simple entertainment.
questions.chinese: 人们可以换件事做，而不是一直刷手机。散步、聊天或完成一项小任务，都可能有所帮助。有时无聊也意味着当前活动缺乏意义，因此选择有明确目标的事情，比如学习技能，可能比单纯娱乐更有效。

questions.title: 去过的无聊地方
questions.text: Why are some teachers’ classes boring? Are there any solutions?
questions.english: Some classes are boring because the teacher talks for too long without involving students. The material may also feel disconnected from real life. Teachers could use shorter explanations, practical examples and small discussions. However, entertainment alone is not enough; students still need to understand the subject and have a chance to ask questions.
questions.chinese: 有些课无聊，是因为老师讲得太久，没有让学生参与。教材也可能与实际生活脱节。老师可以缩短讲解，增加实际例子和小组讨论。不过，仅仅有趣还不够，学生仍需理解内容，并有机会提问。

questions.title: 去过的无聊地方
questions.text: Why do some young people feel bored when talking with old people?
questions.english: There may be a gap in interests or ways of expressing ideas. Young people might want to discuss current entertainment, while older people prefer memories or family matters. That does not mean older people are boring. If both sides ask questions and find a shared interest, the conversation can become much more engaging.
questions.chinese: 双方的兴趣或表达方式可能存在差距。年轻人可能想谈当下的娱乐，老人则更喜欢往事或家庭话题。这不意味着老人本身无聊。如果双方主动提问，找到共同兴趣，聊天就能更吸引人。

questions.title: 去过的无聊地方
questions.text: Do most people think news about celebrities is boring?
questions.english: I would not assume that most people find it boring. Some enjoy following actors or singers because they admire their work. Others lose interest when reports focus on private arguments rather than achievements. I think the quality of the story matters: an interesting interview can be worthwhile, whereas repeated gossip quickly becomes tiresome.
questions.chinese: 我不会认为大多数人都觉得名人新闻无聊。有些人喜欢关注演员或歌手，因为欣赏他们的作品。另一些人在报道只关注私人争执而非成就时会失去兴趣。我认为内容质量很重要：有意思的采访值得看，重复的八卦则容易让人厌倦。

questions.title: 早起经历
questions.text:
Describe a time when you got up early
You should say:
When it was
What you did
Why you got up early
And how you felt about it
questions.english:
A time I got up early was during my solo trip to Europe in June. I needed to catch a morning train, so I set an alarm for around six and prepared most of my things the night before.

After waking up, I checked my documents, packed the remaining items, and made sure I had the information I needed for the journey. I then left early enough to find the correct platform without rushing. Because I was travelling alone, I had to keep track of those details myself.

I got up early mainly to give myself a safety margin. In an unfamiliar place, finding the entrance or understanding a sign can take longer than expected. I thought it was better to have extra waiting time than feel anxious about missing the train.

At first, I felt sleepy and would have preferred to stay in bed. Once everything was ready, though, I felt calmer. The experience made me appreciate preparation: an early start is much easier when there aren't lots of small decisions left to make. I wouldn't want to wake up that early every day, but for that journey it felt like a sensible choice.
questions.chinese:
我早起的一次经历，是在六月独自去欧洲旅行的时候。当时我需要赶一班早上的火车，所以把闹钟设在大约六点，并在前一天晚上准备好了大部分东西。

起床后，我检查了证件，装好剩下的物品，并确认自己掌握了旅途中需要的信息。之后我提早出发，这样就有足够时间找到正确的站台，不用匆忙赶路。因为是独自旅行，这些细节都需要我自己留意。

我早起主要是为了给自己留出一些余量。在陌生的地方，找入口或看懂一个标识，都可能比预期花更长时间。我觉得，多等一会儿比担心错过火车更好。

起初，我有些困，更想继续躺在床上。不过，等一切准备好之后，我就平静多了。这次经历让我体会到提前准备的价值：当没有很多小决定留到最后再做时，早出发会容易得多。我并不想每天都那么早起，但对那次行程来说，这是个合理的选择。
pending: 六月欧洲独行已确认；赶早班火车、约六点起床、前晚准备、具体动作与感受为候选。火车站城市未知，不指定城市。

questions.title: 早起经历
questions.text: Do you know anyone who likes to get up early?
questions.english: Someone with a regular exercise or work routine is the kind of person that comes to mind. They may enjoy having quiet time before the day gets busy. That quiet start can make a demanding day feel less rushed. I can understand the appeal: an early start leaves time for breakfast and a calmer journey.
questions.chinese: 我想到的是有规律运动或工作作息的人。他们可能喜欢在一天忙起来之前享受安静时间。这种安静开局能让繁忙的一天不那么匆忙。我理解早起的吸引力：留出吃早餐的时间，出门也更从容。
pending: 用户认识的早起人士未提供；此稿未声称有特定朋友。

questions.title: 早起经历
questions.text: Why do people get up early?
questions.english: People get up early for practical reasons, such as work, school or a long journey. Others choose to exercise before their responsibilities begin. The morning can also feel quieter, which helps some people concentrate. Still, getting up early is useful only if they sleep enough; losing sleep would cancel out many of the benefits.
questions.chinese: 人们早起可能是为了工作、上学或长途出行。也有人选择在开始处理日常事务前运动。早晨还可能比较安静，有助于一些人集中注意力。不过，早起只有在睡眠充足时才有用，缺觉会抵消不少好处。

questions.title: 早起经历
questions.text: What kinds of occasions need people to arrive early?
questions.english: Flights, job interviews and important examinations are obvious examples. Arriving early gives people time to find the right place and deal with unexpected delays. It can also show respect when others are waiting. I would allow a reasonable buffer, though, rather than arrive so early that I interrupt preparations or make the host uncomfortable.
questions.chinese: 乘飞机、求职面试和重要考试都是明显的例子。提前到达让人有时间找到正确地点、应对意外延误，也能体现对等候者的尊重。不过，我会留出合理的缓冲时间，而不是早到打断准备工作，或让主人不自在。

questions.title: 早起经历
questions.text: Why do some people like to stay up late?
questions.english: Some people feel more alert at night, especially when the surroundings become quiet. Others stay up because of work, entertainment or conversations with friends. The problem is not simply the clock time, but whether their schedule allows enough sleep. Staying up late regularly becomes unhealthy if they still have to get up very early.
questions.chinese: 有些人晚上更清醒，尤其是在周围安静下来后。另一些人则因为工作、娱乐或与朋友聊天而熬夜。问题不只是睡觉的钟点，而是作息能否保证充足睡眠。如果仍需很早起床，长期晚睡就不健康。

questions.title: 早起经历
questions.text: Is it good to arrive early in any situation?
questions.english: Not in every situation. Being early is sensible for an examination or a train, because missing it has clear consequences. But arriving much earlier than agreed at someone's home may inconvenience the host. I think punctuality means considering the situation and other people's schedules, not always trying to be the first person there.
questions.chinese: 并非任何场合都适合。考试或赶火车时提前到达很合理，因为错过会有明确后果。但去别人家时比约定早很多，可能会给主人添麻烦。我认为守时应考虑具体情况和他人的安排，而不是总想第一个到。

questions.title: 早起经历
questions.text: What kind of people like getting up early?
questions.english: People who enjoy a quiet start or have regular morning commitments may prefer it. For example, someone who exercises before work can make that activity part of a routine. However, I would not link early rising automatically with success. Different people have different energy patterns, and getting sufficient sleep matters more than copying someone else's timetable.
questions.chinese: 喜欢安静开局、或早晨有固定安排的人，可能偏好早起。例如，在上班前运动的人，可以把运动纳入固定作息。不过，我不会把早起自动等同于成功。每个人的精力规律不同，睡够比照搬他人的时间表更重要。

questions.title: 喜欢在家/花园种菜的人
questions.text:
Describe a person who loves to grow plants (e.g. vegetables, flowers) at home or in
the garden
You should say:
Who this person is
What plants he/she grows
How he/she grows the plants
And explain why he/she loves growing plants
questions.english:
A person who enjoys growing plants is my mother. We live together in an apartment in Guangdong, where a few small pots can fit comfortably.

She grows mint and a few flowering plants near a window where they can receive light. The plants aren't arranged as a perfect display. She pays attention to each one, checks the soil, and changes the position of a pot if it seems to need more sunlight.

Her approach is patient and practical. She waters them when necessary rather than following a rigid rule every day. When a plant produces new leaves, she notices the change and enjoys seeing that her care has made a difference. The routine is small, but it gives the room a more lively atmosphere.

I think she likes growing plants because it offers a calm activity with visible progress. Unlike many tasks on a computer, the result develops slowly and can't simply be rushed. I enjoy technology, so I find that contrast interesting. It also shows how someone can create a little contact with nature without needing a house or a large outdoor space.
questions.chinese:
喜欢种植物的一个人是我的母亲。我们一起住在广东的一套公寓里，屋里可以摆下几个小花盆。

她在能够晒到阳光的窗边种了薄荷和几盆开花的植物。她并没有把这些植物布置成一套完美的陈列，而是会留意每一盆的状态，检查土壤；如果某盆植物似乎需要更多阳光，她就会挪动它的位置。

她照料植物的方式很耐心，也很实际。她在植物需要时浇水，而不是每天机械地遵循同一个规则。当植物长出新叶，她会注意到变化，也很高兴看到自己的照料起了作用。这只是一个小小的日常习惯，却让房间更有生气。

我觉得她喜欢种植物，是因为这是一项安静的活动，而且能看到进展。与许多电脑上的任务不同，植物的变化慢慢发生，不能简单地催促。我喜欢技术，所以觉得这种对比很有趣。这也说明，即使没有独栋房子或很大的户外空间，人们仍然可以与自然建立一点联系。
pending: 母亲同住广东公寓已确认；种植爱好、薄荷花卉、窗边摆放、照料方式和动机全部为授权候选。

questions.title: 喜欢在家/花园种菜的人
questions.text: What are the advantages of growing vegetables or flowers at home?
questions.english: Growing plants can make a home more attractive and give people a relaxing activity away from screens. Vegetables may also provide a small amount of fresh food. For children, watching a plant grow makes patience and responsibility easier to understand. It takes space and care, though, so the benefits depend on what a household can manage.
questions.chinese: 种植物可以让家更好看，也提供远离屏幕、放松身心的活动。蔬菜还能带来少量新鲜食物。对孩子而言，观察植物生长让耐心和责任感更容易理解。不过，种植需要空间和照料，收益取决于家庭能够承担的程度。

questions.title: 喜欢在家/花园种菜的人
questions.text: Do many people grow vegetables or flowers at home in your country?
questions.english: Some people in China do grow flowers or vegetables at home, but the available space makes a big difference. A house with a garden allows larger plants, while apartment residents might keep a few pots on a balcony. I would not claim that everyone does it; personal interest, time and sunlight all affect the choice.
questions.chinese: 中国确实有人在家种花或种菜，但可用空间影响很大。有花园的房子能种较大的植物，公寓居民可能只在阳台放几个花盆。我不会说人人都这样做，个人兴趣、时间和光照都会影响选择。

questions.title: 喜欢在家/花园种菜的人
questions.text: Is it easy to grow plants at home?
questions.english: It depends on the plant and the conditions at home. A hardy plant can be fairly easy to keep if it has enough light and appropriate watering. Growing vegetables successfully may take more attention. Beginners should start with something manageable rather than buy many plants at once, because regular care matters more than initial enthusiasm.
questions.chinese: 这取决于植物以及家里的环境。耐养的植物只要光线和浇水合适，就比较容易养。想成功种出蔬菜可能需要更多照料。新手应从容易管理的植物开始，而不是一次买很多，因为持续照料比最初的热情更重要。

questions.title: 喜欢在家/花园种菜的人
questions.text: Why do some people like to grow plants?
questions.english: For some people, it is a relaxing hobby with a visible result. They can watch something develop gradually instead of dealing only with tasks on a screen. Others enjoy making their surroundings greener or sharing vegetables with family. The attraction is not necessarily saving money; caring for a living thing can be rewarding in itself.
questions.chinese: 对一些人而言，这是有可见成果的放松爱好。他们可以观察事物逐渐生长，而不是只处理屏幕上的任务。也有人喜欢让环境更绿，或与家人分享蔬菜。吸引力未必在于省钱，照料生命本身就可能让人有满足感。

questions.title: 喜欢在家/花园种菜的人
questions.text: Why do some people prefer to grow their own fruits and vegetables instead of buying them from the market?
questions.english: They may value freshness and enjoy knowing how their food was grown. It can also be satisfying to eat something they have cared for themselves. However, home growing does not automatically mean cheaper or safer food. People still need suitable soil, water and sensible methods, so I see it as both a hobby and a practical activity.
questions.chinese: 他们可能看重新鲜度，也喜欢了解食物的种植过程。吃到自己照料长成的食物，还会有满足感。不过，自己种不自动意味着更便宜或更安全，仍需合适的土壤、水和合理方法。因此，我认为它兼具爱好和实用活动的性质。

questions.title: 喜欢在家/花园种菜的人
questions.text: Do you think students should learn to grow plant?
questions.english: Yes, a small growing project can teach students where food comes from and why living things need care. It also gives science lessons a practical side. Schools do not need a large garden; a few suitable containers could work. The aim should be understanding and responsibility, rather than expecting every student to become an expert gardener.
questions.chinese: 可以。小型种植项目能让学生了解食物来源，以及生命为什么需要照料，也让科学课更贴近实践。学校不必有大花园，几个合适的容器就能尝试。目标应是理解和责任感，而不是让每位学生都成为园艺专家。

questions.title: 想颁布的新法律
questions.text:
Describe a new law you would like to introduce in your country
You should say:
What law it is
What changes this law brings
Whether this new law will be popular
How you came up with the new law
And explain how you feel about this new law
questions.english:
A new law I would like to propose is a stronger, simpler requirement for apps to explain and limit their use of personal data. China already has privacy rules, so I wouldn't describe privacy protection as a completely new idea.

The additional requirement would be a standard permission screen written in clear language. An app would have to explain what information it needs, why it needs it, and how users can withdraw permission. Refusing unnecessary access shouldn't prevent someone from using the basic service.

I think this could make people more confident about using technology. It might be popular with users who feel confused by long terms and conditions, although some companies could dislike the extra work. Proper enforcement would matter as much as the wording of the law.

The idea came from thinking about how easily people click through permission requests without understanding them. As an AI student, I'm interested in useful systems, but usefulness shouldn't depend on collecting everything possible. I would feel positive about a rule that makes the choices clear and keeps data collection proportionate. It would help technology serve people while allowing them more control over their own information.
questions.chinese:
我想提议的一项新法律，是要求应用以更有力、更简单的方式说明并限制个人数据的使用。中国已经有隐私保护规则，因此我不会把隐私保护说成一个全新的想法。

我希望新增的要求，是一个使用清晰语言的标准权限页面。应用必须解释需要哪些信息、为什么需要，以及用户怎样撤回授权。用户拒绝不必要的访问权限，不应妨碍他们使用基本服务。

我认为，这可能让人们更有信心使用技术。它也许会受到那些被冗长条款弄得一头雾水的用户欢迎，不过一些公司可能不喜欢由此增加的工作。法律能否得到切实执行，与条文本身同样重要。

这个想法来自我的思考：人们很容易在并不理解权限请求的情况下，直接点击通过。作为人工智能专业的学生，我对有用的系统感兴趣，但系统有用不应该以尽可能收集所有信息为前提。我会支持让选择更清楚、让数据收集保持适度的规则。这样既能让技术服务于人，也能让人们更好地掌控自己的信息。
pending: 这是一项观点提案，非现行法条解读或真实政策；用户是否持此观点待确认，不声称中国完全没有相关法律。

questions.title: 想颁布的新法律
questions.text: What rules should students follow at school?
questions.english: Students should follow rules that protect learning and safety, such as arriving on time, treating others respectfully and doing their own work. Rules against bullying are particularly important. However, schools should explain the reasons instead of demanding blind obedience. Students are more likely to take a rule seriously when they understand whom it protects.
questions.chinese: 学生应遵守维护学习和安全的规则，比如准时到校、尊重他人、独立完成作业。禁止欺凌尤其重要。不过，学校应解释理由，而不是要求盲目服从。学生理解规则在保护谁时，更可能认真遵守。

questions.title: 想颁布的新法律
questions.text: Do people in your country usually obey the law?
questions.english: I think people generally try to follow the law, although compliance varies with the situation. Clear rules and fair enforcement make cooperation easier. Some violations happen through carelessness or a lack of understanding, while others are deliberate. Rather than make a claim about everyone, I would focus on improving legal awareness and making enforcement consistent.
questions.chinese: 我认为人们通常愿意守法，但遵守情况因情境而异。清晰的规则和公平执法有助于配合。有些违法源于粗心或不了解规定，也有些是故意的。与其概括所有人，我更关注提升法律意识和保持执法一致。

questions.title: 想颁布的新法律
questions.text: What kinds of behavior are considered as good behavior?
questions.english: Good behaviour usually involves considering how our actions affect other people. Being honest, keeping promises and respecting shared spaces are simple examples. It also means helping when it is reasonable, rather than only avoiding punishment. Standards may differ slightly between cultures, but treating people fairly and taking responsibility for mistakes are valuable in most situations.
questions.chinese: 良好行为通常意味着考虑自己的行动会如何影响他人。诚实、守信、尊重公共空间都是简单例子。它也包括在合理情况下帮助他人，而不只是躲避惩罚。文化标准可能略有不同，但公平待人、为错误负责，在多数场合都很有价值。

questions.title: 想颁布的新法律
questions.text: Do you think children can learn about the law outside of school?
questions.english: Certainly. Parents can explain everyday examples, such as why people must follow traffic rules or respect someone else's property. Libraries and suitable educational programmes can also help. The information needs to match children's age. I would prefer clear examples and conversations to frightening stories, because understanding a law is more useful than simply fearing punishment.
questions.chinese: 当然可以。家长可以解释日常例子，比如为何遵守交通规则、尊重他人财产。图书馆和合适的教育节目也有帮助。内容应符合孩子的年龄。我更倾向于清楚的例子和交流，而非吓人的故事，因为理解法律比单纯害怕惩罚更有用。

questions.title: 想颁布的新法律
questions.text: What are the benefits for people to obey rules?
questions.english: Rules make people's behaviour more predictable, which helps them share roads, workplaces and public services. Following them can reduce conflict and protect people who have less power. Of course, the rules need to be fair and useful. Obedience is easier to justify when the rule serves a clear purpose rather than someone's personal convenience.
questions.chinese: 规则让行为更可预测，有助于人们共享道路、工作场所和公共服务。遵守规则可以减少冲突，并保护弱势者。当然，规则本身必须公平、有用。当它服务于清楚的公共目的，而不是某个人的便利时，服从才更合理。

questions.title: 想颁布的新法律
questions.text: How can parents teach children to obey rules?
questions.english: Parents should set a good example and keep their expectations clear. If adults ignore a rule themselves, children may not take it seriously. Explaining the reason and using consistent consequences can help. Children should also be allowed to ask questions, because learning to behave responsibly is more valuable than following instructions without any understanding.
questions.chinese: 家长应以身作则，把要求讲清楚。如果大人自己不守规则，孩子可能也不会认真对待。解释原因，并保持后果处理的一致性，会有帮助。也应允许孩子提问，因为学会负责任，比毫无理解地照指令做更有价值。

questions.title: 发小
questions.text:
Describe a friend from your childhood
You should say:
Who he/she is
Where and how you met each other
What you often did together
And explain what made you like him/her
questions.english:
A childhood friend I would like to talk about is a classmate from primary school in my hometown, a small county town in north-eastern China. We first met when we sat near each other in class and began talking during breaks.

We often spent time together after lessons. Sometimes we exchanged books or discussed something we had watched. On other days, we simply walked home and talked about what had happened at school. We didn't need an expensive activity to have a good time.

What I liked most was that they were easy to talk to. If I wasn't ready to speak, they didn't force me to join a noisy conversation. But when we were comfortable together, we could talk for a long time about small things. They also had a sense of humour that made an ordinary school day feel lighter.

The friendship was important because it gave me a familiar person outside my family. We could share interests and help each other when a school task felt difficult. Looking back, I value the simple consistency of it: seeing someone regularly, listening to them, and gradually building trust. That's still the kind of friendship I find most comfortable.
questions.chinese:
我想谈的一位童年朋友，是家乡小学里的一位同学。我的家乡是中国东北的一个小县城。我们最初认识，是因为上课时座位离得很近，课间便开始聊天。

放学后，我们经常一起待一会儿。有时会交换书，或者讨论看过的内容。还有些时候，我们只是一起走回家，聊聊学校里发生的事。不需要参加昂贵的活动，我们也能过得很开心。

我最喜欢的一点，是与对方聊天很自在。如果我一时不想开口，对方不会逼我加入热闹的谈话。但当我们相处得很放松时，也能围绕小事聊很久。对方还有幽默感，让普通的上学日也显得轻松些。

这段友谊很重要，因为它让我在家人之外还有一个熟悉的人。我们可以分享兴趣，遇到难做的学习任务时也会互相帮助。回头看，我珍惜的是这种简单而稳定的相处：经常见面、倾听彼此、慢慢建立信任。这仍然是让我最自在的一种友谊。
pending: 小学朋友、见面方式、换书与步行、幽默互助和儿童阶段具体性格为候选；没有真实朋友姓名或已确认童年事件。

questions.title: 发小
questions.text: Do you still keep in touch with your friends from childhood? Why or why not?
questions.english: If a childhood friendship still feels meaningful, I would like to keep in touch, even when distance makes meetings difficult. Shared memories can make a conversation feel comfortable. At the same time, I would not maintain contact only out of obligation. Friendships need some current connection as well as history, otherwise they can gradually become less close.
questions.chinese: 如果童年友谊仍有意义，我愿意保持联系，即使距离让见面变得困难。共同回忆能让交流很自在。不过，我不会只因为义务而联系。友谊既需要历史，也需要当下的联系，否则可能逐渐疏远。
pending: 是否仍与童年朋友保持联系未提供；此稿不声称已有联系频率。

questions.title: 发小
questions.text: How important is childhood friendship to children?
questions.english: Childhood friendships give children opportunities to share, negotiate and deal with disagreements outside the family. A reliable friend can also make school feel less stressful. However, having one or two good friends may be enough; popularity is not the main goal. The important thing is that the relationship feels safe and both children are treated respectfully.
questions.chinese: 童年友谊让孩子有机会在家庭之外学习分享、协商和处理分歧。可靠的朋友也能减轻上学的压力。不过，有一两个好朋友可能就足够了，受欢迎不是主要目标。关键是关系让人有安全感，双方都得到尊重。

questions.title: 发小
questions.text: What do you think of communicating via social media?
questions.english: Social media is convenient for keeping in touch across distance and sharing small updates. It can help people arrange meetings or find others with similar interests. But short messages lack tone, and constant notifications can become distracting. I see it as a useful tool, provided people choose when to use it and do not let it replace every conversation.
questions.chinese: 社交媒体方便远距离联系、分享近况，也能帮助安排见面或结识兴趣相近的人。但短消息缺少语气，持续通知还会分散注意力。我把它看作有用的工具，前提是主动选择使用时间，不让它取代所有交流。

questions.title: 发小
questions.text: Do you think online communication through social media will replace face-to-face communication?
questions.english: I do not think it will replace face-to-face communication completely. Online messages are useful when people live far apart, but meeting in person gives us body language and a fuller sense of someone's feelings. Some conversations also need privacy and attention. The two methods can support each other rather than compete for every part of our social lives.
questions.chinese: 我认为它不会完全取代面对面交流。人们相隔很远时，网上消息很有用，但见面能让我们看到肢体语言，更完整地感受对方的情绪。有些谈话也需要隐私和专注。两种方式可以互相支持，而不是争夺社交生活的每一部分。

questions.title: 发小
questions.text: What's the difference between having younger friends and older friends?
questions.english: Older friends may offer experience and a different perspective on decisions. Younger friends can introduce new interests or ways of using technology. However, these are possibilities rather than fixed rules. I would value someone who listens and treats me fairly, regardless of age, because shared values and mutual respect matter more than an age difference.
questions.chinese: 年长朋友可能提供经验，以及看待决定的不同角度。年轻朋友可能带来新兴趣或技术使用方式。不过，这些只是可能性，不是固定规则。不论年龄，我都重视愿意倾听、公平待我的人，因为共同价值观和相互尊重比年龄差更重要。

questions.title: 发小
questions.text: Has technology changed people's friendships? How?
questions.english: Yes, technology has made it easier to maintain friendships over long distances. People can exchange messages, share photos or have a video call without arranging a journey. It also helps them meet people with similar interests. The downside is that easy contact can stay quite shallow, so close friendships still need time, attention and genuine support.
questions.chinese: 是的，技术让远距离维持友谊更容易。人们不必安排出行，就能发消息、分享照片或视频通话，也更容易结识兴趣相近的人。缺点是方便的联系可能停留在表面，因此亲密友谊仍需要时间、关注和真正的支持。

questions.title: 想从事医疗行业的人
questions.text:
Describe a person you know who would like to choose a career in the medical field
(e.g. a doctor, a nurse)
You should say:
When you knew him/her
When he/she started to think about that
What he/she would like to do
And explain why he/she would like to choose this career
questions.english:
Someone I know who wants to become a nurse is a former schoolmate. I got to know them at secondary school, and we stayed in touch enough to discuss our future plans.

They started thinking seriously about the medical field near the end of school, when choosing what to study became more immediate. They were interested in science, but they also wanted work that involved direct contact with people rather than only studying information from a distance.

Their goal is to train as a nurse and work in a hospital. What attracts them is the practical side: noticing what a patient needs, explaining simple information clearly, and working with other professionals. They understand that the job can involve difficult schedules and responsibility, so it isn't simply an idealized picture of helping people.

I think the choice suits the qualities they want to develop. They are patient and prefer doing something concrete when someone needs support. My own direction is AI and robotics, so our paths are different. But I can understand the wish to connect knowledge with real situations. I would hope they choose it after learning enough about the everyday work, not just because the title sounds respectable.
questions.chinese:
我认识的一位想成为护士的人，是我以前的一位同学。我们在中学认识，后来也一直保持着一定联系，会聊到彼此的未来计划。

临近中学毕业、需要考虑接下来学什么的时候，对方开始认真考虑医疗行业。对方对科学有兴趣，同时也希望做一份能直接与人接触的工作，而不是只在远处研究相关信息。

对方的目标是接受护理培训，然后在医院工作。吸引对方的是这份工作的实际内容：留意患者的需求、清楚解释简单的信息，以及与其他专业人员合作。对方知道这份工作可能有辛苦的排班，也要承担责任，所以并不只是把帮助他人想象得很美好。

我觉得这个选择符合对方想培养的品质。对方很耐心，别人需要支持时，也更愿意做些具体的事。我的方向是人工智能和机器人，所以我们的道路不同，但我能理解把知识与真实情况联系起来的愿望。我希望对方在充分了解日常工作之后再选择这条路，而不只是因为这个职业听起来很体面。
pending: 医疗职业同学、认识时间、志向形成时间、性格动机和联系均为完整候选；不声称有真实医疗行业朋友或已获入学资格。

questions.title: 想从事医疗行业的人
questions.text: Do you think being a doctor is easy or difficult?
questions.english: I think it is difficult, both academically and emotionally. Doctors need extensive knowledge, practical training and the ability to make careful decisions under pressure. They also communicate with people who may be frightened or in pain. Good equipment helps, but it does not remove that responsibility. The work can be rewarding precisely because it matters so much.
questions.chinese: 我认为很难，无论在学业还是情感层面。医生需要广泛知识、实践训练，以及在压力下谨慎决策的能力，还要与可能害怕或疼痛的人交流。好的设备有所帮助，却不能消除责任。这份工作很有意义，也正因为它如此重要。

questions.title: 想从事医疗行业的人
questions.text: Do you think learning biology is interesting for children?
questions.english: Biology can be very interesting when children see its connection with the world around them. Learning how a plant grows or how animals adapt is easier to enjoy than memorising isolated terms. Teachers could use observations and simple experiments. Not every child will love the subject, but practical activities give more children a reason to be curious.
questions.chinese: 当孩子看见生物学与周围世界的联系时，它会很有意思。了解植物如何生长、动物如何适应环境，比背孤立术语更容易让人感兴趣。老师可以使用观察和简单实验。并非每个孩子都会喜欢，但实践活动能让更多孩子产生好奇心。

questions.title: 想从事医疗行业的人
questions.text: Why do some children want to become doctors?
questions.english: Some children admire the idea of helping people recover from illness. Others may be inspired by a family member, a teacher or a programme about hospitals. The job can also appear respected and meaningful. As children grow older, they need to learn about the long training and responsibilities as well, so their choice becomes more informed.
questions.chinese: 有些孩子向往帮助人们康复，也有人受到家人、老师或医院相关节目的启发。这份工作还可能显得受尊重、有意义。随着长大，他们也需要了解漫长的培训和责任，让职业选择建立在更充分的认识上。

questions.title: 想从事医疗行业的人
questions.text: Do you think governments should put a large amount of money into medical research?
questions.english: Yes, medical research deserves substantial support because it can improve prevention, diagnosis and treatment. Some useful projects take years and may not attract immediate private investment. However, funding should be reviewed carefully and shared with essential health services. Research has the greatest value when its results are reliable and can eventually help patients in practice.
questions.chinese: 应该支持，因为医学研究能改善预防、诊断和治疗。有些有用项目需要多年，未必能立即吸引私人投资。不过，资金分配应谨慎评估，也要兼顾基本医疗服务。当成果可靠，并最终能实际帮助患者时，研究的价值最大。

questions.title: 想从事医疗行业的人
questions.text: Why is some doctors’ pay high and others’ low?
questions.english: Pay can differ because doctors have different experience, qualifications and responsibilities. A specialist may spend many years developing a particular skill, while working conditions also vary between hospitals and regions. Demand can influence income too. However, a lower salary does not mean a doctor contributes less, so pay should also consider workload and public need.
questions.chinese: 医生的经验、资质和责任不同，收入就可能不同。专科医生可能多年培养某项技能，医院和地区间的工作条件也不一样，需求也会影响收入。不过，收入低不意味着贡献小，薪酬也应考虑工作量和公共需要。

questions.title: 想从事医疗行业的人
questions.text: Do you think doctors should be paid more?
questions.english: Doctors should receive fair pay that reflects their training, workload and responsibility. Where conditions are difficult or staffing is inadequate, better pay may help retain skilled people. But money alone will not solve every problem. Reasonable working hours, professional support and safe conditions are also necessary if we want doctors to provide consistently good care.
questions.chinese: 医生应获得与培训、工作量和责任相匹配的公平薪酬。条件困难或人员不足时，提高收入可能帮助留住人才，但钱无法解决所有问题。合理工时、专业支持和安全条件也不可缺少，才能让医生持续提供良好照护。

questions.title: 拥有成功商业的人
questions.text:
Describe a person you know who has a successful business
You should say:
Who this person is
How you got to know him/her
Why and how he/she started the business
What business he/she does
And explain why you think the business is successful
questions.english:
Someone I know with a successful business is a family acquaintance who runs a small computer repair and support shop. I got to know them when they helped someone in my family with a device problem.

They started the business because they had technical experience and noticed that local customers needed help they could understand. Instead of focusing only on selling new equipment, the shop deals with repairs, setup problems, and basic advice about using computers safely.

At the beginning, they kept the service range fairly small and relied on careful work and recommendations. What stands out is their way of explaining a problem. They tell customers what is necessary, what can wait, and whether repairing a device is actually worthwhile. That makes people feel less worried about being charged for something they don't need.

I think the business is successful because customers return and recommend it to others. Success here isn't about becoming a huge company immediately. It is about earning a stable reputation and solving everyday problems reliably. As someone interested in computing, I appreciate the combination of technical knowledge and communication. A repair is more useful when the customer also understands how to avoid the same issue again.
questions.chinese:
我认识的一位生意做得很成功的人，是家里的一位熟人，对方经营一家小型电脑维修与技术支持店。当时家人遇到了设备问题，得到了对方的帮助，我也因此认识了这位店主。

对方开店，是因为有技术经验，也注意到本地顾客需要能够听懂的帮助。店里并不只专注于卖新设备，也会处理维修、设置问题，并提供安全使用电脑的基础建议。

刚开始时，对方把服务范围控制得比较小，主要依靠认真做事和他人推荐。最突出的地方，是解释问题的方式。对方会告诉顾客哪些处理是必要的、哪些可以等等，以及这台设备到底值不值得修。这让顾客不必那么担心被收取不必要的费用。

我认为这门生意成功，是因为顾客会回来，也会推荐给别人。这里的成功并不是马上变成一家大公司，而是建立稳定的口碑，可靠地解决日常问题。我对计算机感兴趣，因此很欣赏技术知识与沟通能力的结合。如果顾客也能理解怎样避免同样的问题再次发生，那么这次维修就更有价值。
pending: 经营者及认识方式、开店经过、服务做法、回头客和成功评价均为完整候选；不写真实收入或已核验商业成果。

questions.title: 拥有成功商业的人
questions.text: Why do some people start their own business?
questions.english: Some people want independence and the chance to put their own ideas into practice. Others see an unmet need and believe they can offer a better product or service. Owning a business can also bring financial rewards, but the risks are real. It usually requires handling uncertainty, expenses and responsibilities that an employee may not face.
questions.chinese: 有人想独立，并把自己的想法付诸实践，也有人发现未被满足的需求，相信能提供更好的产品或服务。创业还可能带来财务回报，但风险真实存在，通常要处理员工未必面对的不确定性、费用和责任。

questions.title: 拥有成功商业的人
questions.text: Should governments provide financial support to start-ups?
questions.english: Governments can support promising start-ups, especially when a useful project struggles to attract funding. However, support should have clear conditions and checks, rather than reward every new company automatically. Training, advice and access to shared facilities may sometimes help more than cash. The aim should be creating lasting value, not keeping weak businesses alive indefinitely.
questions.chinese: 政府可以支持有潜力的初创企业，尤其是有用项目难以融资时。但支持需要明确条件和监督，而不是自动奖励所有新公司。培训、建议和共享设施，有时比现金更有效。目标应是创造长期价值，而非无限维持弱势企业。

questions.title: 拥有成功商业的人
questions.text: Do most people prefer shopping at big stores or small stores?
questions.english: I think the preference depends on what people need. Large stores can offer a wider selection and convenient comparison, while small shops may provide more personal service or specialised products. Price, distance and trust also matter. Someone might buy everyday supplies from a supermarket but choose a small local shop for a particular repair or unusual item.
questions.chinese: 我认为偏好取决于需求。大店选择更多、方便比较，小店则可能提供更贴心的服务或专门产品。价格、距离和信任也重要。有人会在超市买日用品，却到本地小店维修，或购买特别的物品。

questions.title: 拥有成功商业的人
questions.text: What makes a business successful?
questions.english: A successful business needs to understand a real customer need and deliver something consistently useful. Good financial management matters because even a popular product can fail if costs are uncontrolled. Staff and reliable service are important too. I think lasting success comes from earning trust and adapting sensibly, rather than chasing every new trend without a clear purpose.
questions.chinese: 成功企业需要了解真实需求，并持续提供有用的东西。财务管理也重要，因为成本失控时，再受欢迎的产品也可能失败。员工和可靠服务同样关键。我认为长期成功来自赢得信任和合理适应，而非没有方向地追逐每个潮流。

questions.title: 拥有成功商业的人
questions.text: What makes a business fail?
questions.english: A business may fail when it offers something customers do not really need or cannot afford. Poor cash management and expanding too quickly can create problems as well. Competition and unexpected changes also matter. Failure is not always caused by laziness; sometimes the original idea needs testing earlier so the owner can change direction before losing too much.
questions.chinese: 企业可能因为提供顾客不需要、或买不起的东西而失败。现金管理不当、扩张过快也会出问题，竞争和意外变化也有影响。失败不一定源于懒惰，有时应更早测试想法，让经营者在损失过大之前调整方向。

questions.title: 拥有成功商业的人
questions.text: Is it easy to set up a new business in your country?
questions.english: It depends on the kind of business. A small service business may need less initial money than a factory or a heavily regulated activity. In China, finding customers and managing competition can still be challenging even when the basic setup is manageable. I would distinguish opening a business from making it sustainable; the second task is usually harder.
questions.chinese: 取决于业务类型。小型服务业的启动资金可能低于工厂或监管严格的行业。在中国，即使基本设立过程可以处理，寻找顾客和应对竞争仍可能很难。我会区分开业和持续经营，后者通常更困难。

questions.title: 近期改变的计划
questions.text:
Describe a plan that you had to change recently
You should say:
When this happened
What made you change the plan
What the new plan was
And how you felt about the change
questions.english:
A plan I had to change was a weekend visit to a park with a friend. We had arranged it a few weeks ago because we both wanted a break from studying and thought a long walk would be relaxing.

On the morning of the visit, the weather became very rainy. We could have continued, but walking around outside no longer seemed enjoyable or convenient. We talked briefly and decided to choose an indoor activity instead of cancel everything.

The new plan was to meet at a library and then have something to eat nearby. We each looked for a book and spent some quiet time reading before talking over a meal. It was a different kind of break, but still gave us time away from our normal tasks.

At first, I was disappointed because I had been looking forward to fresh air. Once we changed the plan, I felt better. I like reading, and I'm more talkative with familiar people, so the alternative suited me quite well. The experience reminded me that the purpose of a plan can matter more than its exact details. We wanted to relax together, and that was still possible.
questions.chinese:
我曾经改过一个计划：周末和朋友去公园。几周前，我们约好了这次出行，因为都想从学习中暂时放松一下，觉得走一段长路会很舒服。

出行当天早上下起了大雨。我们本来可以照常出发，但在户外散步已经不太愉快，也不方便。简单商量之后，我们决定改成室内活动，而不是取消整个计划。

新的安排是在图书馆见面，然后去附近吃点东西。我们各自找了一本书，安静地读了一会儿，再边吃饭边聊天。虽然休息的方式变了，我们仍然得以暂时放下平时的任务。

起初我有些失望，因为一直期待出去呼吸新鲜空气。调整安排后，我的心情好了些。我喜欢阅读，而且在熟悉的人面前比较健谈，所以这个替代方案也很适合我。这次经历让我意识到，计划的目的有时比具体细节更重要。我们想一起放松一下，而这个目的仍然实现了。
pending: 周末朋友计划、几周前、雨天、图书馆与用餐经过及感受为授权候选；不声称真实天气或行程。

questions.title: 近期改变的计划
questions.text: Do people often change their plans?
questions.english: Yes, plans often change because people receive new information or circumstances turn out differently from expected. An appointment may move, a deadline may change, or a better option may appear. Adjusting a plan is not necessarily a sign of poor organisation. The important thing is to know which goals should stay fixed and which details can remain flexible.
questions.chinese: 会。人们获得新信息，或情况与预期不同时，计划常会改变。预约可能调整、截止时间可能变化，也可能出现更好的选项。调整计划不一定意味着组织不善，关键是知道哪些目标应保持，哪些细节可以灵活改变。

questions.title: 近期改变的计划
questions.text: Would you tell others if you change your plan?
questions.english: Yes, if the change affects someone else, I would let them know as soon as possible. That gives them time to adjust their own arrangements and avoids unnecessary waiting. I would also explain the new plan clearly. For something entirely private, an announcement is not needed, but commitments involving other people should be handled with consideration.
questions.chinese: 如果变化影响他人，我会尽快告知，让他们有时间调整自己的安排，也避免无谓等待。我还会清楚说明新计划。完全私人的事情无需宣布，但涉及他人的承诺应体贴地处理。

questions.title: 近期改变的计划
questions.text: Why do you think parents still make plans for their children nowadays?
questions.english: Parents often want to protect their children from mistakes and help them prepare for the future. They may also feel that their own experience gives them a useful perspective. However, planning everything can prevent children from becoming independent. I think parents should discuss options and explain risks, while gradually allowing children to make age-appropriate choices themselves.
questions.chinese: 家长常想保护孩子免于犯错，并帮助准备未来，也可能觉得自身经验能提供有用视角。但包办所有计划会妨碍孩子独立。我认为家长应讨论选项、解释风险，同时逐步让孩子自主作出符合年龄的选择。

questions.title: 近期改变的计划
questions.text: How does technology help people make plans?
questions.english: Digital calendars can help people see deadlines and avoid conflicting appointments. Maps and booking platforms make travel plans easier, while shared documents help a group coordinate tasks. Still, technology cannot decide priorities for us. It is useful when the plan is clear, but adding too many reminders or complicated tools can make a simple task harder.
questions.chinese: 电子日历帮助查看截止时间，避免预约冲突。地图和预订平台让旅行计划更容易，共享文档帮助团队协调任务。不过，技术不能替我们决定优先级。计划清晰时工具有用，但过多提醒或复杂工具反而让简单任务更难。

questions.title: 近期改变的计划
questions.text: What kind of plans do people often make?
questions.english: People make short-term plans for daily tasks, meetings and shopping, as well as longer plans for education, careers or major purchases. The level of detail should match the situation. A simple list may be enough for a weekend, while studying abroad requires several stages. Plans are most useful when they connect a clear goal with realistic next steps.
questions.chinese: 人们为日常任务、会面和购物做短期计划，也为教育、职业或大额购买做长期计划。详细程度应适合具体情况：周末可能只需简单清单，留学则需多个阶段。当计划把明确目标与现实的下一步连接起来时，最有用。

questions.title: 近期改变的计划
questions.text: Do you think people like the process of making plans more, or the moment of carrying them out?
questions.english: Different people enjoy different parts. Planning can be exciting because it allows them to imagine possibilities without facing difficulties yet. Carrying out the plan may be more satisfying because it produces a real result. Personally, I would value both, but I think a plan only proves useful when someone actually takes the steps needed to make it happen.
questions.chinese: 不同的人喜欢不同环节。规划让人想象各种可能，还不用面对困难，因此可能很令人兴奋。执行产生实际结果，可能更有满足感。我会重视两者，但只有真正采取必要步骤，计划才能证明自己的价值。

questions.title: 在团队中工作
questions.text:
Describe a time when you worked in a group
You should say:
What you did
Who you worked with
What problems you faced
And explain why you worked in the group
questions.english:
A time I worked in a group was during a university project related to robotics. I worked with three other students, and our aim was to create a small demonstration in which a robot responded to information from a computer program.

We divided the work according to our strengths. Some people focused on the robot's movement, while others dealt with the program and testing. I helped with the coding and tried to make the information passed between the different parts clear.

The main difficulty was that each part could work separately but still fail when we combined them. We had also made different assumptions about the format of the data. To deal with that, we agreed on a simple shared example and tested one connection at a time. Regular short discussions helped us notice problems before they became larger.

We worked as a group because the task required more than one type of knowledge, and sharing the work made it manageable. I found the process useful because I had to explain my thinking instead of only solve problems privately. I'm fairly quiet, but a clear task gives me something concrete to contribute. The experience showed me that cooperation includes careful listening as well as technical ability.
questions.chinese:
我参加团队工作的一次经历，是大学里的一个机器人项目。我与另外三名学生合作，目标是做一个小型演示，让机器人能够根据电脑程序传来的信息作出反应。

我们按照各自的优势分工。有些人负责机器人的运动，另一些人负责程序和测试。我帮忙写代码，并努力让不同部分之间的信息传递更清楚。

主要困难是，每个部分单独都能工作，但组合起来仍然可能出问题。我们对数据格式也作出了不同的假设。为了解决这个问题，我们确定了一个简单的共同示例，每次只测试一个连接。定期进行简短讨论，也帮助我们在问题变大之前就发现它们。

我们之所以组队，是因为任务需要不止一种知识，而分担工作能让任务更容易处理。我觉得这个过程很有用，因为我必须解释自己的思路，而不只是独自解决问题。我比较安静，但明确的任务让我有具体的事情可以贡献。这次经历让我看到，合作不仅需要技术能力，也需要认真倾听。
pending: 机器人团队项目、四人、分工、接口问题和解决经过全部为授权候选；不宣称真实项目、已完成机器人演示或掌握技能。

questions.title: 在团队中工作
questions.text: Why do some people prefer to work by themselves?
questions.english: Working alone gives people more control over their time and methods. It can also make concentration easier when a task requires detailed thinking. Some people find group discussions slow or stressful. However, independent work has limits: without feedback, mistakes may go unnoticed. I think the best choice depends on whether the task needs individual focus or several different skills.
questions.chinese: 独立工作让人更能控制时间和方法，也有助于在需要细致思考时集中注意力。有些人觉得小组讨论缓慢或有压力。不过，缺少反馈时，错误可能被忽视。我认为应看任务更需要个人专注，还是多种不同技能。

questions.title: 在团队中工作
questions.text: What should a leader do to make team members want to follow him or her?
questions.english: A leader should make the purpose clear, listen to the team and treat people fairly. Members are more willing to cooperate when their work feels useful and their concerns are taken seriously. The leader also needs to keep promises and accept responsibility. Giving orders may produce short-term compliance, but trust is what encourages people to contribute willingly.
questions.chinese: 领导应明确目标、倾听团队、公平待人。当工作有意义、顾虑被认真对待时，成员更愿意合作。领导也应守信、承担责任。命令可能带来短期服从，但信任才让人自愿贡献。

questions.title: 在团队中工作
questions.text: Should students learn to do group work?
questions.english: Yes, because many real tasks require people with different skills to cooperate. Group work can teach students to explain ideas, share responsibilities and handle disagreement. However, it should be organised carefully so one person does not do everything. Teachers need to assess individual contributions as well as the final result, otherwise the lesson may simply become unfair.
questions.chinese: 应该，因为许多实际任务需要不同技能的人合作。小组活动可以教学生表达想法、分担责任、处理分歧，但应合理组织，避免一个人包办。老师既要评价个人贡献，也要看最终成果，否则学习活动可能变得不公平。

questions.title: 在团队中工作
questions.text: What group tasks are there in schools?
questions.english: Schools can organise science projects, presentations, sports activities or discussions in small groups. Each task gives students a slightly different way to cooperate. For example, a presentation involves researching, organising information and speaking clearly. The task should have a shared goal and identifiable roles, so students practise teamwork rather than simply sit together while working separately.
questions.chinese: 学校可以组织小组科学项目、展示、体育活动或讨论，每种任务训练的合作方式略有不同。例如，展示涉及查资料、整理信息和清楚表达。任务应有共同目标和明确角色，让学生真正练合作，而不是坐在一起各做各的。

questions.title: 在团队中工作
questions.text: What advantages are there for students experiencing teamwork at school?
questions.english: Teamwork gives students practice in explaining ideas and listening to views they may not share. They can learn to divide a large task and combine different strengths. It also reveals how important reliability is when others depend on them. These lessons can be useful later at university or work, provided the group experience is fairly organised.
questions.chinese: 团队合作让学生练习表达，也学习倾听自己未必认同的看法。他们能学会拆分大任务、结合不同优势，也会发现他人依赖自己时，可靠性有多重要。只要小组安排公平，这些经验对未来大学或工作都有用。

questions.title: 在团队中工作
questions.text: How can you tell if a person is a good leader?
questions.english: I would look at how the person behaves when something goes wrong. A good leader listens, identifies the problem and helps the team move forward instead of blaming everyone. They also give credit fairly and make decisions transparently. Confidence is useful, but it is not enough; the team's trust and the quality of cooperation are better indicators.
questions.chinese: 我会看出问题时这个人如何应对。好领导会倾听、识别问题，帮助团队前进，而不是责怪所有人。他们也会公平认可贡献、透明决策。自信有用，但不够；团队的信任和合作质量是更好的判断标准。

questions.title: 重要决定
questions.text:
Describe an important decision that you made
You should say:
What the decision was
How you made your decision
What the results of the decision were
And explain why it was important
questions.english:
An important decision I made was to plan for a PhD abroad. I started thinking seriously about that goal about a year ago, and it has become a direction for what I want to do after my master's degree.

My current subject is artificial intelligence, especially robotics. When considering the next step, I thought about both the research I wanted to pursue and the kind of education I hoped to experience. Studying abroad appealed to me because I wanted to broaden my perspective and learn in a more varied environment.

I made the decision by comparing it with the option of ending my formal studies after the master's. I considered the time and effort involved, rather than only the attractive parts. The result so far is a clearer goal and a reason to take my English preparation seriously.

The decision matters because I want to deepen my research in embodied AI and help bring general-purpose intelligent robots into real-world use. That is a long-term aim, and I know it will involve difficult work. Having a direction doesn't remove that uncertainty, but it helps me choose what to focus on. For me, the importance lies in connecting further education with a purpose I genuinely care about.
questions.chinese:
我作出的一个重要决定，是计划去海外读博士。大约一年前，我开始认真考虑这个目标，而它已经成为我硕士毕业后的一个发展方向。

我现在的专业是人工智能，尤其关注机器人。考虑下一步时，我既思考了想继续开展什么研究，也思考了希望接受怎样的教育。海外学习吸引我，是因为我希望拓宽视野，在更加多元的环境中学习。

作决定时，我把这条路与硕士毕业后不再继续正规学业的选择作了比较。我考虑了需要投入的时间和精力，而不只是它有吸引力的一面。目前的结果是，目标更加清晰，也让我有理由认真对待英语备考。

这个决定很重要，因为我希望深化具身智能研究，帮助通用智能机器人走向实际应用。这是一个长期目标，我知道其中会有艰难的工作。有了方向并不能消除不确定性，但能帮助我决定把注意力放在哪里。对我来说，它的重要性在于把继续深造与一个我真正关心的目标联系起来。
pending: 海外博士意向、约一年规划、动机及具身智能研究方向已确认；具体比较决策过程和主观结果是候选。当前结果只写目标与准备，不写录取、申请已提交或已完成博士成果。

questions.title: 重要决定
questions.text: Do you think children sometimes have to make important decisions?
questions.english: Yes, children sometimes make choices that matter to them, such as choosing friends, joining an activity or deciding how to respond to bullying. Adults should not dismiss these decisions as trivial. Children need guidance that matches their age, but also opportunities to think for themselves. A small decision can have a significant effect on their confidence or wellbeing.
questions.chinese: 会，比如选择朋友、参加活动，或决定如何应对欺凌，这些选择对孩子很重要。成人不应把它们当作小事。孩子需要符合年龄的指导，也需要独立思考机会。看似小的决定可能显著影响信心或身心状态。

questions.title: 重要决定
questions.text: What important decisions do teenagers need to make after graduation?
questions.english: They may need to decide whether to continue studying, enter training or look for work. If they continue their education, choosing a subject and a place to study can be important. These choices affect money, time and future opportunities. I think teenagers should compare realistic options and seek advice, while remembering that a first choice is not always permanent.
questions.chinese: 他们可能需要决定继续学习、接受职业培训，还是找工作。如果继续读书，专业和学习地点也很重要。这些选择影响金钱、时间和未来机会。我认为应比较现实选项、寻求建议，同时记得首次选择并不总是永久的。

questions.title: 重要决定
questions.text: Who can children turn to for help when making a decision?
questions.english: Children can ask parents, teachers or another trusted adult who understands the situation. Friends can provide emotional support, but may not have enough experience for every decision. The adult should explain options rather than immediately choose for the child. That way, the child receives help while still developing the confidence and skills needed to make decisions independently.
questions.chinese: 孩子可以问父母、老师，或了解情况的可信成年人。朋友能提供情感支持，但未必对所有决定都有足够经验。成年人应解释选项，而不是立即代选。这样孩子既获得帮助，也培养独立决策所需的信心和技能。

questions.title: 重要决定
questions.text: Do you think advertisements can influence our decisions when shopping?
questions.english: Yes, advertisements can make a product more familiar and highlight benefits we might not have considered. Repeated exposure may also make a brand feel trustworthy even before we try it. That does not mean the product is the best choice. I think shoppers should compare useful information, prices and actual needs rather than rely only on the advert.
questions.chinese: 会。广告让产品更熟悉，也突出我们未曾考虑的优点。反复接触还可能让品牌在试用前就显得可信，但这不意味着它就是最佳选择。我认为购物者应比较有效信息、价格和实际需要，而非只依赖广告。

questions.title: 重要决定
questions.text: Do you think the influence of advertising is good?
questions.english: It can be positive when advertising helps people discover a useful product or understand its features. The problem comes when it exaggerates results or creates pressure to buy unnecessary things. Children may be particularly vulnerable to that pressure. So I would support honest, clear advertising, alongside consumer education and reasonable limits on misleading claims.
questions.chinese: 广告帮助人们发现有用产品、理解功能时，影响可以是积极的。夸大效果、制造购买不必要物品的压力时，就会出问题，孩子尤其容易受影响。因此，我支持诚实清楚的广告，也重视消费教育和对误导宣传的合理限制。

questions.title: 重要决定
questions.text: How do people usually make important decisions?
questions.english: People often start by identifying the options and considering possible consequences. They may gather information, discuss the choice with someone they trust and compare short-term and long-term effects. Emotions matter as well, but I would avoid deciding only under pressure. For an important decision, allowing time to check assumptions can prevent a mistake that is difficult to reverse.
questions.chinese: 人们通常先找出选项、考虑后果，再收集信息，与可信的人讨论，并比较短期和长期影响。情绪也重要，但我会避免只在压力下作决定。面对重要选择，花时间检查假设，可以避免难以挽回的错误。

questions.title: 喜欢的现场体育赛事
questions.text:
Describe a live sports event you watched and liked
You should say:
What it was
When and where you watched it
Who you watched it with
And explain why you liked it
questions.english:
A live sports event I enjoyed was a basketball match between two student teams at university. I watched it last semester on a campus court with two classmates.

It wasn't a professional competition with famous athletes, but there was a lively atmosphere. Supporters stood near the court, and it was easy to see the players communicating and reacting to what happened. Because we were there in person, the changes in pace felt more immediate than they would on a screen.

The match stayed fairly close, so neither side could relax. One team played more carefully near the end, passed the ball patiently, and created a good chance instead of rushing. I liked watching how the players adjusted their decisions under pressure.

I enjoyed the event because it combined a clear shared goal with teamwork. I didn't need to be an expert to appreciate a well-timed pass or someone helping a teammate recover from a mistake. Going with familiar classmates also made the experience comfortable. We could talk about the game afterwards without turning it into a loud social occasion. For me, it was an enjoyable break from studying and a practical example of cooperation happening in real time.
questions.chinese:
我喜欢的一次现场体育赛事，是大学里两支学生队伍之间的篮球比赛。上学期，我和两位同学在校园球场观看了这场比赛。

它并不是有著名运动员参加的职业比赛，但现场气氛很活跃。支持者站在场边，我们可以很清楚地看到球员怎样交流、怎样对场上的情况作出反应。因为是在现场，比赛节奏的变化比隔着屏幕观看更直接。

双方的比分一直很接近，所以谁都不能放松。有一支队伍在接近结束时打得更加谨慎，耐心传球，创造出一个好机会，而不是急着出手。我喜欢观察球员怎样在压力下调整自己的决策。

我喜欢这场比赛，是因为它把明确的共同目标与团队合作结合起来。即使不是专家，我也能欣赏一次时机恰好的传球，或者队友怎样帮助失误的球员重新调整。和熟悉的同学一起去，也让我感到自在。赛后我们可以聊聊比赛，而不必把它变成一场吵闹的社交活动。对我来说，这既是学习之余一次愉快的休息，也是在现场看到团队合作展开的具体例子。
pending: 校园现场篮球观看、上学期、两同学、赛况与喜欢原因全为授权候选。明确live现场而非电视或网络直播；不虚构用户看过正式大赛。

questions.title: 喜欢的现场体育赛事
questions.text: Why do some people like to watch sports events?
questions.english: Sports events combine competition, uncertainty and a shared atmosphere. People enjoy seeing skilled athletes perform, and supporting a team gives them something to discuss with others. A close match can also be exciting because the outcome is not predictable. For some viewers, it is a social activity as much as an interest in the sport itself.
questions.chinese: 体育赛事结合了竞争、不确定性和共同氛围。人们喜欢看优秀运动员表现，支持球队也提供与他人交流的话题。势均力敌的比赛因结果难预测而令人兴奋。对一些观众而言，它既是体育兴趣，也是社交活动。

questions.title: 喜欢的现场体育赛事
questions.text: Where do people normally watch sports events?
questions.english: People can watch at the venue, at home or in a place where friends gather around a screen. Watching at home is convenient and usually easier to fit into a schedule. A stadium offers a stronger atmosphere, but involves travel and tickets. The choice depends on cost, access and whether someone values the live experience.
questions.chinese: 人们可以到现场、在家，或和朋友聚在屏幕前观看。在家很方便，也通常更容易融入日程。体育场的氛围更强，但需要出行和门票。选择取决于成本、便利程度，以及是否重视现场体验。

questions.title: 喜欢的现场体育赛事
questions.text: What are the advantages of watching sports events online?
questions.english: Online viewing allows people to follow a match without travelling to the venue. They may also have access to replays, commentary and different camera angles, which can make the action easier to understand. It is convenient for events in another country. However, the experience depends on a stable connection and does not fully reproduce the atmosphere of a crowd.
questions.chinese: 网上观看让人不必前往现场，也可能提供回放、解说和不同镜头角度，让赛事更容易理解。对于国外的比赛尤其方便。不过，体验依赖稳定网络，也无法完全再现人群的现场氛围。

questions.title: 喜欢的现场体育赛事
questions.text: What sports matches are suitable for children to attend?
questions.english: I would choose events with a safe environment, clear rules and a manageable length. A local school competition or a family-friendly professional match could be suitable. Children should be able to see what is happening and leave if they become tired. The behaviour of spectators matters too, because a hostile crowd can spoil the experience.
questions.chinese: 我会选环境安全、规则清楚、时长适中的比赛。本地学校比赛或适合家庭的职业赛事都可以。孩子应看得清比赛，累了也能离场。观众的行为同样重要，因为充满敌意的人群会破坏体验。

questions.title: 喜欢的现场体育赛事
questions.text: Why do some people spend a lot going to other countries to watch sports events?
questions.english: For dedicated fans, attending a major event can feel like a special experience rather than an ordinary purchase. They may want to see a favourite team, share the atmosphere or combine the match with travel. The cost reflects that emotional value. Still, I think the decision should fit their budget rather than create financial pressure afterwards.
questions.chinese: 对忠实球迷来说，重大赛事是一种特别体验，而非普通消费。他们可能想看喜欢的球队、感受氛围，或把比赛和旅行结合起来。投入反映了这种情感价值。不过，我认为应量力而行，避免之后产生经济压力。

questions.title: 喜欢的现场体育赛事
questions.text: What sports games are popular in your country?
questions.english: Basketball, football and table tennis are examples of sports that attract attention in China. People may enjoy playing a sport themselves or following major competitions. Preferences vary with age, local facilities and personal interests, so I would not give a precise ranking. An accessible place to play can influence popularity as much as famous athletes do.
questions.chinese: 篮球、足球和乒乓球都是在中国受到关注的运动。人们可能自己参与，也可能关注大型赛事。偏好因年龄、当地设施和兴趣而异，因此我不会给出精确排名。便利的运动场地与知名运动员一样，也能影响受欢迎程度。

questions.title: 特别场合的食物
questions.text:
Describe a food that people eat on special occasions/events
You should say:
What it is
What the special event/occasion is
How it is cooked/made
And explain why people eat it on that special occasion/event
questions.english:
I'd like to talk about dumplings, which are associated with the Spring Festival in many families in China, especially in the north. They are small parcels of filling wrapped in thin pieces of dough, and they can be served as part of a family meal.

To make them, people prepare a filling, often with vegetables and meat, although there are many different versions. A small amount is placed in the centre of a wrapper, and the edges are pressed together carefully so the filling stays inside. The dumplings can then be boiled, steamed or cooked in a pan, depending on the style.

One reason they suit a special occasion is that making them can be a shared activity. Several people can prepare the wrappers, fill them and talk at the same time. Dumplings are also associated with reunion and good wishes, so their meaning goes beyond their taste.

I think they are a good example of how ordinary ingredients become part of a tradition. The food feels special because of the occasion and the people sharing it, rather than because it is especially expensive.
questions.chinese:
我想谈饺子。在中国许多家庭，尤其北方家庭，饺子与春节联系紧密。它是用薄面皮包住馅料的小面食，可以成为家庭餐的一部分。

制作时先准备馅料，通常有蔬菜和肉，但也有很多不同版本。把少量馅放在面皮中央，仔细捏合边缘，避免馅漏出来。根据不同做法，之后可以煮、蒸或用平底锅烹制。

它适合特别场合的一个原因，是制作过程可以一起完成。几个人能够做面皮、包馅，同时聊天。饺子还与团聚和祝福关联，所以意义不只在味道。

我认为它很好地说明普通食材如何成为传统的一部分。食物之所以显得特别，是因为享用的场合和一起分享的人，而不是因为它特别昂贵。

questions.title: 特别场合的食物
questions.text: Why are there special foods on special occasions or events?
questions.english: Special foods help people recognise an occasion and connect it with shared memories. Some dishes also carry symbolic meanings, such as togetherness or good wishes. Preparing and eating them can bring a family together. The food does not have to be expensive; its value often comes from the tradition and the people who share it.
questions.chinese: 特别食物帮助人们辨认节日，并连接共同记忆。有些菜还象征团聚或祝福。准备和享用它们可以让家人聚在一起。食物不必昂贵，其价值往往来自传统以及共同分享的人。

questions.title: 特别场合的食物
questions.text: What are the differences between everyday food and festival food?
questions.english: Everyday food is usually chosen for convenience, nutrition and cost. Festival food may involve more preparation, a particular tradition or dishes that are shared with a larger group. It can feel special because people do not eat it so often. However, the distinction is not absolute; a familiar simple dish can also become meaningful on a celebration day.
questions.chinese: 日常食物通常考虑方便、营养和成本。节日食物可能准备更费工、承载传统，或适合更多人分享。因为不常吃，它会显得特别。不过，界限并不绝对，熟悉简单的菜也能在庆祝日具有特别意义。

questions.title: 特别场合的食物
questions.text: Are there any differences between the food people eat today and the food people ate in the past?
questions.english: Many people now have access to a wider range of ingredients and meals from different places. Refrigeration, transport and online delivery can also change how food reaches the table. In the past, choices often depended more on local and seasonal supplies. Still, traditional dishes remain important, so change does not mean that older food habits simply disappear.
questions.chinese: 如今很多人能接触更丰富的食材和各地菜肴。冷藏、运输和线上配送也改变食物上桌的方式。过去的选择往往更依赖本地和季节供应。不过，传统菜仍然重要，变化并不意味着旧饮食习惯直接消失。

questions.title: 特别场合的食物
questions.text: Do people today prefer eating at home or in a restaurant?
questions.english: It depends on time, budget and the occasion. Eating at home gives people more control over ingredients and may be cheaper, while a restaurant is convenient and can feel special. Some people use both options during the same week. I would avoid claiming a single preference for everyone, because a busy weekday and a family celebration create different needs.
questions.chinese: 取决于时间、预算和场合。在家吃更能控制食材，也可能更便宜；餐馆则方便，还能带来特别体验。有些人一周内两种方式都会用。我不会概括所有人的偏好，因为忙碌工作日和家庭庆祝需要不同。

questions.title: 擅长学习和说语言的人
questions.text:
Describe a person who is good at learning and speaking new languages
You should say:
How you got to know him/her
How he/she learns a new language
What languages he/she can speak
And explain how you feel about him/her
questions.english:
The person I'd like to describe is a fellow student from my master's programme. I first got to know him during a discussion after a university seminar, when we discovered that we both enjoyed reading and Japanese animation.

He speaks Chinese and English, and he can also communicate in Japanese. What impresses me is not simply the number of languages, but the way he keeps improving them. He reads short texts, listens to material he finds interesting and tries to use new expressions in conversation. Instead of memorising a long list and forgetting it, he returns to useful words in different situations.

He is also comfortable asking someone to correct him. If he cannot remember a word, he explains the idea another way rather than ending the conversation. That makes his speaking feel natural, even when it is not perfect.

I admire his patience and consistency. Learning a language can seem like an enormous task, but he turns it into small activities he can repeat. I would like to take that approach to my own English preparation, because regular use seems more practical than waiting until I feel completely ready.
questions.chinese:
我想描述硕士项目里的一位同学。大学一次讲座后的讨论中，我们发现都喜欢阅读和日本动漫，于是认识了。

他会中文、英语，也能用日语交流。让我佩服的不是单纯会几种语言，而是持续进步的方式。他读短文、听感兴趣的材料，尝试在交流中使用新表达。他不是背完一长串单词就忘掉，而是在不同情境反复接触有用词语。

他也愿意请别人纠正。如果想不起某个词，会换种方式解释，而不是结束谈话。因此，即使不完美，表达也显得自然。

我欣赏他的耐心和持之以恒。学习一门语言可能看起来是项艰巨的任务，他却把它变成可重复的小活动。我也想把这种方法用于英语备考，因为经常实际使用英语，比等到自己觉得完全准备好更实际。
pending: 该同学、相识经过、语言能力和学习习惯均为候选故事，尚未确认。

questions.title: 擅长学习和说语言的人
questions.text: Are there many people who can speak foreign languages in your country?
questions.english: English is taught widely in China, so many people have some knowledge of it. However, studying a language and communicating confidently are not the same thing. Opportunities to practise vary considerably. Other foreign languages are studied too, particularly when people have academic, work or personal interests connected with them, so I would avoid treating language ability as uniform.
questions.chinese: 中国广泛教授英语，因此许多人有一定英语知识。但学过语言与能自信交流不是一回事，练习机会差异很大。也有人学习其他外语，尤其是出于相关的学术、工作或个人兴趣。因此，我不会把语言能力看作完全一致。

questions.title: 擅长学习和说语言的人
questions.text: Does speaking other languages help at work?
questions.english: Yes, another language can help someone communicate with colleagues, clients or researchers from different countries. It may also provide access to information that has not been translated. However, language skill alone does not guarantee career success. It works best alongside professional knowledge and the ability to explain ideas clearly, rather than being treated as a substitute for expertise.
questions.chinese: 有帮助。另一种语言让人能与不同国家的同事、客户或研究者交流，也能获取尚未翻译的信息。但语言能力本身不保证职业成功。它应结合专业知识和清楚表达的能力，而不是代替专业技能。

questions.title: 擅长学习和说语言的人
questions.text: Do people learn any languages other than English?
questions.english: Yes, people may study Japanese, Korean, French or other languages for different reasons. Some enjoy films, books or music, while others need a language for study or work. English is useful internationally, but it is not the only valuable choice. Motivation and regular practice often matter more than simply choosing the language with the largest number of learners.
questions.chinese: 会，人们可能因不同理由学习日语、韩语、法语等。有些喜欢电影、书或音乐，另一些因学习或工作需要而学。英语在国际上有用，但并非唯一有价值的选择。动机和规律练习往往比单纯选最多人学的语言更重要。

questions.title: 擅长学习和说语言的人
questions.text: Why is it easier for children to learn new things than for adults?
questions.english: Children often have fewer responsibilities and more opportunities to practise through play. They may also worry less about making mistakes. However, I would not say adults are always slower; adults can use prior knowledge and effective strategies. The difference depends on the skill, the teaching method and how much time each person can spend practising.
questions.chinese: 孩子通常责任较少，也有更多通过玩耍练习的机会，可能更不怕犯错。不过，我不会说成人总学得慢，成人可以利用已有知识和有效策略。差异取决于技能、教学方法，以及能投入多少练习时间。

questions.title: 擅长学习和说语言的人
questions.text: How do people learn new things?
questions.english: People usually combine instruction, observation and practice. A clear explanation provides a starting point, but trying the task reveals what they do not yet understand. Feedback then helps them improve. For example, learning to programme requires actually writing and testing code. I think small, repeated attempts are often more effective than consuming large amounts of information without using it.
questions.chinese: 人们通常结合讲解、观察和练习。清楚的说明提供起点，实际尝试则暴露尚未理解的部分，反馈帮助继续改进。例如，学编程需要真正写代码并测试。我认为小规模重复尝试，往往比大量接收却不使用信息更有效。

questions.title: 擅长学习和说语言的人
questions.text: What is the most important thing for learning a language well?
questions.english: I think the most important thing is using the language regularly in meaningful situations. Memorising words helps, but learners also need to listen, speak, read and write with a purpose. Feedback is useful because repeated mistakes can become habits. A routine that is realistic and sustainable usually matters more than studying intensely for a few days and then stopping.
questions.chinese: 我认为最重要的是在有意义的情境中规律使用语言。背词有帮助，但也需有目的地听、说、读、写。反馈很有用，因为重复错误可能形成习惯。现实、能持续的规律，通常比猛学几天后停止更重要。

questions.title: 遇到的科技问题
questions.text:
Describe a challenging technological problem you faced
You should say:
What the problem was
When and where you faced it
How challenging it was
And explain how you solved it
questions.english:
A technological problem I'd describe involved a programme that suddenly stopped working on my laptop. It was related to a small robotics project, and I noticed the problem while working at home one afternoon.

The programme had worked before, but after a software update it produced an error as soon as I started it. At first, I did not know whether the problem was in my own code or in one of the packages it depended on. That uncertainty made it frustrating, because changing several things at once could make the situation even harder to understand.

I decided to work through it systematically. I read the error message carefully, checked what had changed and tested a much smaller piece of code. That helped me identify a mismatch between package versions. I created a separate environment, installed compatible versions and ran the small test again before returning to the whole programme.

The programme finally worked, and I felt relieved. More importantly, the experience showed me why it helps to keep clear notes and isolate a problem instead of guessing. It was challenging, but it became manageable once I broke it into steps.
questions.chinese:
我想描述一次笔记本上程序突然不能运行的问题。它与小型机器人项目有关，是某天下午在家工作时发现的。

程序原先正常，软件更新后，一启动就报错。开始不清楚是自己的代码，还是依赖的软件包出了问题。这种不确定令人烦躁，因为同时改很多地方可能让问题更难理解。

我决定按步骤检查：认真阅读错误信息、检查哪些地方发生了变化，并测试一段更小的代码。这帮助找到软件包版本不匹配。我创建独立环境，安装兼容版本，先运行小测试，再回到完整程序。

程序终于正常，我松了口气。更重要的是，这让我认识到记录清楚、隔离问题比猜测更有帮助。虽然困难，但拆成步骤后就能处理。
pending: 项目、报错、更新、排查步骤及发生时间地点均为候选事件，未登记为用户真实经历。

questions.title: 遇到的科技问题
questions.text: What are the advantages and disadvantages of AI?
questions.english: AI can process information quickly and help with repetitive tasks, which gives people more time for complex work. It can also support learning and accessibility. However, its output may be inaccurate or biased, and collecting data can raise privacy concerns. I think the benefits depend on careful design, human checking and clear responsibility when the system makes mistakes.
questions.chinese: AI能快速处理信息、帮助完成重复任务，为复杂工作留出时间，也能支持学习和无障碍使用。但输出可能不准确或有偏见，数据收集也可能引发隐私问题。我认为收益取决于谨慎设计、人工检查，以及系统出错时明确的责任。

questions.title: 遇到的科技问题
questions.text: Do you think people today should learn about AI technology?
questions.english: Yes, people should understand the basic capabilities and limits of AI, even if they do not become specialists. They need to know that a confident answer can still be wrong and that personal information deserves care. Basic knowledge helps them decide when a tool is useful, when to check its output and when a human should remain responsible.
questions.chinese: 应该，即使不成为专家，也应了解AI的基本能力和局限。人们需要知道，自信的回答仍可能出错，个人信息也应谨慎处理。基础知识帮助判断何时工具有用、何时核查输出，以及何时应由人继续承担责任。

questions.title: 遇到的科技问题
questions.text: Should children learn to use AI?
