questions.english: Children can learn to use suitable AI tools with guidance, but they should first develop their own thinking and basic skills. A tool might explain a difficult idea or suggest practice, rather than complete every assignment for them. Teachers and parents need to discuss accuracy and privacy. The goal should be learning with assistance, not avoiding the effort of learning.
questions.chinese: 孩子可以在指导下使用合适的AI工具，但首先应发展独立思考和基础技能。工具可以解释难点、建议练习，而不是包办全部作业。老师和家长需要讨论准确性与隐私。目标应是辅助学习，而不是绕过学习本身的努力。

questions.title: 遇到的科技问题
questions.text: How can AI help in our lives?
questions.english: AI can help people organise information, translate text and handle some routine tasks. It may also make services easier to use, for example by turning speech into written text. However, a useful assistant should not be trusted automatically. I would check important information and keep people involved when an error could affect someone's health, money or opportunities.
questions.chinese: AI可以帮助整理信息、翻译文本和处理部分常规任务，也能让服务更容易使用，比如把语音转成文字。不过，有用的助手不应被自动信任。我会核查重要信息，在错误可能影响健康、金钱或机会时，保持人的参与。

questions.title: 遇到的科技问题
questions.text: Do you think students are overly reliant on AI?
questions.english: Some students may become overly dependent on AI if they use it to produce answers without understanding them. That makes an assignment look complete while the actual learning remains weak. However, dependence is not inevitable. Asking for feedback after making an independent attempt can be useful. The key is whether the student is still doing the thinking.
questions.chinese: 有些学生只让AI生成答案、不理解内容，就可能过度依赖。作业看似完成，实际学习却薄弱。但依赖并非必然：独立尝试后寻求反馈可能很有用。关键在于学生是否仍在自己思考。

questions.title: 遇到的科技问题
questions.text: What can teachers do to stop students from relying too much on AI?
questions.english: Teachers can ask students to show their reasoning and explain answers in their own words. Short classroom tasks also reveal what they can do without assistance. Instead of only banning AI, teachers should explain acceptable uses and design work that values the process. Feedback on drafts can then support learning without allowing the tool to replace every stage.
questions.chinese: 老师可以要求学生展示推理、用自己的话解释答案。课堂短任务也能显示他们在没有辅助时会做什么。与其只禁AI，不如说明合理用法，设计重视过程的任务。对草稿提供反馈，则能辅助学习而不替代所有环节。

questions.title: 名人出演的广告
questions.text:
Describe an advertisement with a famous person in it
You should say:
Who the person is
Where you can see it
What the advertisement is about
And explain how you feel about the advertisement
questions.english:
An advertisement I'd like to describe features Yao Ming, the former Chinese basketball player. It is a public-awareness advertisement about protecting sharks rather than selling a normal consumer product. The message is that demand for shark-fin products can lead to harm to these animals.

You can see this kind of campaign material online, including short videos and shared images. The version I have in mind uses a familiar public figure to encourage people to think about what their purchases support. Because Yao Ming is widely recognised, his presence makes the message easier to notice and remember.

What I like is that the advertisement connects an everyday consumer choice with a consequence that may be far away and normally invisible. It does not need a complicated story to make the basic point. However, I think a famous face should draw attention to the issue, not replace evidence or a proper explanation.

Overall, I find it more worthwhile than an advertisement that only encourages unnecessary spending. It tries to change behaviour for a wider purpose, and that makes the celebrity's involvement feel relevant rather than simply decorative.
questions.chinese:
我想描述一则由前中国篮球运动员姚明出演的广告。它宣传保护鲨鱼，而非销售普通消费品，传达的是对鱼翅产品的需求可能伤害这些动物。

这类宣传材料能在网上见到，包括短视频和分享图片。我想到的版本借助熟悉的公众人物，让人思考购买行为在支持什么。姚明广为人知，因此信息更易被注意和记住。

我喜欢它把日常消费选择，与通常看不见、距离很远的后果连接起来，不需要复杂故事就能说明基本道理。不过，我认为名人应吸引关注，而不应取代证据或充分解释。

总体而言，我认为它比只鼓励不必要消费的广告更值得关注。它希望为更广的目的改变行为，因此，名人的参与显得与主题相关，而不只是起装饰作用。
pending: 姚明保护鲨鱼宣传是公共题材；用户实际观看渠道、具体广告版本和态度尚未确认。

questions.title: 名人出演的广告
questions.text: What are the advantages and disadvantages of advertisements?
questions.english: Advertisements help people discover products and give businesses a way to explain what they offer. They can also support services that are free to users. On the other hand, too many adverts are distracting, and misleading claims can waste people's money. Their value depends on whether they provide useful information rather than simply pressure people to buy.
questions.chinese: 广告帮助人们发现产品，让企业解释自己的服务，也能支持对用户免费的服务。另一方面，过多广告分散注意力，误导宣传可能浪费金钱。其价值取决于是否提供有用信息，而不是单纯施压让人购买。

questions.title: 名人出演的广告
questions.text: Why are many advertisements endorsed by celebrities? How useful are they?
questions.english: Celebrities attract attention and make a product easier to remember. A familiar face may also transfer some trust to the brand. That can be useful for awareness, but it does not prove quality. The effect is stronger when the person's image genuinely fits the product; an obviously forced connection may make the advertisement less convincing.
questions.chinese: 名人吸引注意，使产品更易记住，熟悉的面孔也可能把部分信任转移到品牌上。这有助于提高知名度，却不证明质量。人物形象确实适合产品时效果更强，明显生硬的联系反而可能降低说服力。

questions.title: 名人出演的广告
questions.text: What is the most important factor in an advertisement?
questions.english: I think the most important factor is a clear, believable message about why the product is useful. Attractive images can draw attention, but people should understand what is being offered. The advertisement also needs to suit its audience. A memorable slogan is helpful only if it connects with something the company can actually deliver to its customers.
questions.chinese: 我认为最重要的是清楚可信地说明产品为何有用。漂亮画面吸引注意，但人们应理解广告在提供什么。广告也需适合受众。好记的标语只有连接企业真正能交付给顾客的东西时，才有帮助。

questions.title: 名人出演的广告
questions.text: Why are some advertisements boring?
questions.english: Some adverts repeat familiar claims without giving people anything new or useful. Others are too long, poorly targeted or interrupt an activity at the wrong moment. Repetition can make even a creative advert tiring. I think a good advertisement respects attention, communicates quickly and offers a reason to care, rather than relying on noise or constant exposure.
questions.chinese: 有些广告重复老套宣传，没有新信息；有些过长、受众不准，或在不合适时打断活动。反复播放也会让有创意的广告变烦。我认为好广告应尊重注意力、快速传达信息，并给人关心的理由，而非依靠喧闹和持续曝光。

questions.title: 名人出演的广告
questions.text: Is advertising important for a company? Why?
questions.english: Advertising can be important because customers need to know that a company and its products exist. It can explain a new service or help a brand stand out. However, it cannot compensate indefinitely for poor quality. A business also needs satisfied customers and reliable delivery, so advertising should support a good offer rather than disguise a weak one.
questions.chinese: 广告重要，因为顾客首先要知道公司和产品的存在。它能解释新服务、帮助品牌突出，但不能长期弥补低质量。企业还需要满意的顾客和可靠交付，因此广告应支持好的产品，而不是掩饰薄弱的产品。

questions.title: 名人出演的广告
questions.text: Which is more effective, online advertising or offline advertising?
questions.english: Online advertising can reach specific groups and make it easy to find more information or buy immediately. Offline advertising may work better in a local area or for people who use the internet less. Neither is always more effective. The right choice depends on the audience, the product and the message, and sometimes combining the two is sensible.
questions.chinese: 线上广告可以触达特定人群，也方便立即查信息或购买。线下广告可能更适合本地地区或较少上网的人。没有一种总是更有效，应根据受众、产品和信息选择，有时结合两种很合理。

questions.title: 推荐旅行过的地方
questions.text:
Describe a place you have travelled to that you would like to recommend to
others
You should say:
What it is
Where it is
What you saw and did there
And explain why you would like to recommend it to others
questions.english:
A place I'd like to recommend is Vienna, the capital of Austria. I visited it during a solo trip to Europe in June. I went to Europe to attend an academic conference, and I spent more time in Vienna than in Budapest.

While I was in Vienna, I visited the Golden Hall and some local museums. The city has a rich cultural atmosphere, and its distinctive architecture is one of the main things I'd recommend it for. If you enjoy museums and interesting buildings, there is plenty to explore. Trying the local food would also be a way to experience the city's culture and its distinctive flavours.

Overall, I'd describe Vienna as a comfortable city to spend time in. For me, its appeal is the combination of culture, architecture and the overall experience of being there.

One other memory from my European trip has stayed with me. While I was waiting for a train, I chatted with a man who was living on the streets, and I felt that people were very friendly. That conversation made the wider trip memorable as well. So Vienna would be my recommendation, especially for someone interested in culture and museums.
questions.chinese:
我想推荐奥地利首都维也纳。今年六月，我独自赴欧洲旅行时去过那里。这趟欧洲行是为了参加学术会议，而我在维也纳待的时间比布达佩斯更长。

在维也纳，我参观了金色大厅和一些当地博物馆。城市文化氛围浓厚，独特的建筑也是我推荐它的主要原因之一。如果喜欢博物馆和有趣建筑，这里有很多可以探索的地方。尝试当地食物，也是体验城市文化和独特风味的一种方式。

总体而言，我会把维也纳描述为一个待起来舒适的城市。它对我的吸引力，在于文化、建筑和身处其中的整体体验相结合。

欧洲旅行还有一段记忆让我印象深刻。等火车时，我与一位住在街头的人聊天，感觉大家很友好。这次谈话也让整趟旅行难忘。所以，维也纳会是我的推荐，尤其适合对文化和博物馆感兴趣的人。

questions.title: 推荐旅行过的地方
questions.text: Where do people in your country often go for holidays?
questions.english: People in China have many options, from nearby coastal areas and mountains to historic cities or overseas destinations. The choice depends on budget, available time and whether they want relaxation or exploration. Short breaks may be spent closer to home, while longer holidays allow more travel. I would not assume that one type of destination suits everyone.
questions.chinese: 中国人有很多选择，从附近海滨、山地到历史城市或海外目的地。选择取决于预算、时间，以及想休息还是探索。短假可能在家附近度过，长假则能走更远。我不会认为某一种目的地适合所有人。

questions.title: 推荐旅行过的地方
questions.text: What is the ideal length for a holiday?
questions.english: For me, an ideal holiday would be long enough to relax without becoming difficult to afford or arrange. A few days can suit a nearby destination, while a distant trip usually needs more time. Travel itself can be tiring, so I would leave some room to recover. The quality of the break matters more than choosing a fixed number of days.
questions.chinese: 我理想中的假期应长到足以放松，又不至于难以负担或安排。附近旅行几天就合适，远行通常需更久。旅途本身可能累，因此我会留恢复时间。休假质量比规定固定天数更重要。

questions.title: 推荐旅行过的地方
questions.text: How do people usually plan holidays?
questions.english: People usually begin with their budget, available dates and preferred destination. Then they compare transport and accommodation and decide which activities matter most. Reviews and maps can help, but too much searching may become overwhelming. I think a useful plan covers the essentials while leaving some flexibility for weather, delays or an interesting place discovered along the way.
questions.chinese: 人们通常先看预算、可用日期和目的地，再比较交通、住宿，确定最重要的活动。评价和地图有帮助，但搜索过多也会令人不知所措。我认为好计划应覆盖基本事项，并为天气、延误或途中发现的趣处留出弹性。

questions.title: 推荐旅行过的地方
questions.text: Is it important to plan a holiday ahead?
questions.english: Planning ahead is useful for booking transport, finding accommodation and checking entry requirements. It can reduce uncertainty, especially for a trip abroad. However, planning every minute may make the holiday feel like a timetable. I would arrange the parts that are costly or difficult to change, then leave some free time for exploring and resting.
questions.chinese: 提前规划有助于预订交通、寻找住宿、检查入境要求，尤其在出国时能减少不确定性。但安排每一分钟会让假期像一张时间表。我会先落实昂贵或难改变的事项，再留些自由时间探索和休息。

questions.title: 推荐旅行过的地方
questions.text: Why do many countries try to attract people to visit?
questions.english: Visitors spend money on accommodation, food, transport and activities, which can support local jobs and businesses. Tourism also gives a country opportunities to share its culture. However, attracting more visitors is not always better if places become overcrowded or residents are inconvenienced. I think governments should aim for tourism that brings benefits while protecting local life and the environment.
questions.chinese: 游客在住宿、餐饮、交通和活动上消费，能支持当地就业和企业。旅游也让国家有机会分享文化。但如果景点拥挤、居民不便，游客越多未必越好。我认为政府应发展既带来收益、又保护当地生活和环境的旅游。

questions.title: 推荐旅行过的地方
questions.text: How do people decide when to travel?
questions.english: People consider work or study schedules, weather and the cost of transport. Families may also need dates that suit several members. Travelling outside busy periods can be more comfortable, but not everyone has that flexibility. I would choose a time when the practical arrangements work and the destination offers the kind of experience I want.
questions.chinese: 人们会考虑工作或学习安排、天气和交通价格。家庭还需兼顾多位成员的时间。避开高峰可能更舒适，但不是人人能灵活安排。我会选择实际安排可行、目的地能提供想要体验的时候。

questions.title: 喜欢拜访但不想住的家
questions.text:
Describe a home that you like to visit but do not want to live in
You should say:
Where it is
What it is like
Why you like to visit it
And explain why you would not like to live there
questions.english:
A home I enjoy visiting but would not want to live in is a friend's family house outside a busy urban area. It is an older, spacious house with a small garden and a comfortable room where visitors can sit and talk.

The atmosphere is what makes it appealing. Compared with an apartment in a city, there is more room and less noise nearby. When visiting, I can spend time chatting, looking at the plants and simply taking a break from study. It feels like a place where there is no need to rush every activity.

However, visiting for a short time is different from living there permanently. The house is farther from the transport and services I would need regularly. Keeping a larger home and garden in good condition also takes work. As a master's student, I would prefer a daily arrangement that makes study and practical errands easier.

So I can appreciate the house without wanting to make it my own home. I like its quiet atmosphere for a visit, but convenience and manageable responsibilities would matter more when choosing where to live.
questions.chinese:
我喜欢拜访、却不想住的一处家，是朋友位于繁忙城区之外的家庭住宅。房子较老、宽敞，有小花园和让客人坐着聊天的舒服房间。

吸引我的是氛围。与城市公寓相比，它空间更大，附近噪声更少。拜访时可以聊天、看植物，暂时从学习中休息。这里似乎不必赶着完成每件事。

但短期拜访不同于长期居住。房子离我日常需要的交通和服务较远，维护较大的房屋和花园也需要花精力。作为硕士生，我更偏好便于学习和处理日常事务的安排。

所以，我可以欣赏这所房子，却不想把它当自己的家。拜访时喜欢安静氛围，但选择居住地时，生活是否便利、相关事务是否在自己能处理的范围内，显得更重要。
pending: 朋友家庭住宅、位置、花园、拜访活动以及住房偏好均为完整候选细节，未确认。

questions.title: 喜欢拜访但不想住的家
questions.text: Do Chinese people like to visit others’ homes?
questions.english: Visiting relatives or friends at home can be an important way to maintain relationships in China, especially during family occasions. A home visit may feel more personal than meeting in a public place. However, preferences differ and people can be busy. I think arranging a suitable time and respecting the host's space matters more than assuming everyone enjoys surprise visits.
questions.chinese: 在中国，到亲友家拜访是维系关系的重要方式，家庭场合尤其如此，也可能比在公共场所见面更亲切。不过，偏好不同，人们也可能忙碌。我认为约好合适时间、尊重主人空间，比假设人人喜欢突然到访更重要。

questions.title: 喜欢拜访但不想住的家
questions.text: What do Chinese people do when they visit others?
questions.english: Visitors often talk, share a meal or spend time with the family. Tea and snacks may be offered, but the details depend on the household and the occasion. It is considerate to follow the host's lead and avoid making extra work. Offering a small amount of help can be polite, as long as it does not interfere with their arrangements.
questions.chinese: 客人常会聊天、共餐或与家人相处。主人可能提供茶和点心，但具体因家庭和场合而异。体贴的做法是顺着主人安排，避免增加负担。适度帮忙可以显得礼貌，但不应干扰他们的安排。

questions.title: 喜欢拜访但不想住的家
questions.text: What kind of place do people in your country like to live in?
questions.english: People usually want somewhere safe, comfortable and convenient for their daily lives. In a city, access to work, transport and services may be especially important. Some prefer a quieter place with more space, even if the journey is longer. Budget also limits the choice, so I would describe housing preferences as a balance between comfort, location and affordability.
questions.chinese: 人们通常想住得安全、舒适，并方便日常生活。在城市，工作、交通和服务的便利性尤其重要。也有人愿意通勤更久，换取安静和更大空间。预算也有限制，因此住房偏好是在舒适、位置和可负担性之间权衡。

questions.title: 喜欢拜访但不想住的家
questions.text: What's the difference between homes in cities and those in the countryside?
questions.english: City homes are often closer to workplaces, public transport and a wide range of services. They may also have less space or more noise. Homes in the countryside can offer a quieter setting and room outdoors, but access to services may be less convenient. These are general differences, though; the actual experience depends on the particular home and location.
questions.chinese: 城市住宅通常更靠近工作、公共交通和多样服务，但空间可能更小、噪声更多。乡村住宅可能更安静、有户外空间，却未必方便获取服务。不过，这只是一般差别，实际体验仍取决于具体住房和位置。

questions.title: 喜欢拜访但不想住的家
questions.text: What kind of gifts do people usually bring when they visit others?
questions.english: People may bring fruit, tea, snacks or a small gift that suits the host. The choice should consider the occasion and what the person likes, rather than focus only on price. Something easy to share can be particularly useful during a family visit. I would also avoid gifts that create storage problems or an obligation to give something expensive back.
questions.chinese: 人们可能带水果、茶、点心，或适合主人的小礼物。应考虑场合和对方喜好，而非只看价格。家庭拜访时，方便分享的东西尤其有用。我也会避免难存放、或让人觉得必须昂贵回礼的礼物。

questions.title: 喜欢拜访但不想住的家
questions.text: How often do you visit your relatives or friends?
questions.english: For me, the frequency would depend on distance, study commitments and whether the other person is available. I would rather arrange a visit when we can talk properly than meet often but feel rushed. Between visits, messages can help maintain the connection. So I would aim for regular, considerate contact rather than a fixed number of meetings every week.
questions.chinese: 对我而言，频率取决于距离、学习安排和对方是否有空。我更愿意在能好好聊天时拜访，而非频繁见面却匆匆忙忙。两次拜访之间可以通过消息保持联系。因此，我倾向于有规律、体贴的联系，而不是固定每周见几次。
pending: 用户实际拜访亲友频率未提供；本稿描述拟定偏好，不声称过去习惯。

questions.title: 包含动物的故事或书
questions.text:
Describe a story/book with animals in it
You should say:
What animals are in it
What the story/book is about
Why you read the story/book
And explain what you think of this story/book
questions.english:
A book with animals in it that I'd like to describe is The Little Prince. It follows a young prince who leaves his small planet and visits different places before arriving on Earth. Two memorable animals in the story are a fox and a snake.

The fox is especially important because it helps the prince think about friendship and the time we give to someone. The snake appears in a different, more mysterious role. Although the book looks simple at first, the characters encourage readers to consider relationships, responsibility and what makes something meaningful.

I chose to read it because it was short enough to approach without feeling overwhelmed, but had ideas worth returning to. A friend recommended it as more than a children's story, which made me curious to give it a try.

What I find attractive is the contrast between the straightforward language and the questions beneath it. The animals are not just decoration; they help express ideas that might sound too abstract in an ordinary explanation. I would see it as a book to read slowly and think about, rather than rush through for the plot alone.
questions.chinese:
我想描述的有动物的书是《小王子》。故事讲年轻王子离开小星球、访问不同地方，最终来到地球。狐狸和蛇是其中两种令人难忘的动物。

狐狸特别重要，因为它帮助王子思考友谊，以及我们为一个人投入的时间。蛇则扮演更神秘的角色。书起初看似简单，但人物让读者思考关系、责任和什么赋予事物意义。

我选择读它，是因为篇幅短，不让人觉得难以开始，却有值得反复思考的想法。一位朋友推荐，说它不只是儿童故事，让我好奇想试读。

我觉得吸引人的，是直白语言与背后问题的反差。动物不只是装饰，而是帮助表达普通解释中可能过于抽象的想法。我会把它当作值得慢读、思考的书，而非只为情节匆匆读完。
pending: 用户是否读过《小王子》未确认；读过及朋友推荐的叙述均为用户授权的完整候选，不能登记为真实阅读经历。

questions.title: 包含动物的故事或书
questions.text: Should schools teach children about animals?
questions.english: Yes, learning about animals can help children understand the natural world and develop respect for living things. Schools can explain habitats, basic needs and responsible treatment without requiring every child to own a pet. Observations, books and suitable visits can support the lessons. The aim should be curiosity and care, rather than treating animals simply as entertainment.
questions.chinese: 应该。了解动物能帮助孩子理解自然、尊重生命。学校可以讲栖息地、基本需求和负责任的对待方式，不必要求每个孩子养宠物。观察、书籍和合适的参观能支持教学，目标应是好奇和关爱，而非只把动物当娱乐。

questions.title: 包含动物的故事或书
questions.text: Some people think pets should not be kept in cities. What do you think?
questions.english: I would not support a complete ban, but urban pet ownership needs responsibility. Owners should consider space, noise, cleanliness and the animal's needs. Some homes are suitable for certain pets, while others are not. Clear rules can reduce conflict with neighbours, so the issue is how animals are cared for rather than whether a city automatically makes ownership unacceptable.
questions.chinese: 我不支持全面禁止，但城市养宠物需要责任。主人应考虑空间、噪声、卫生和动物需求。有些家庭适合某些宠物，有些不适合。清晰规则可以减少邻里冲突，因此重点是照料方式，而不是城市本身是否让养宠物不可接受。

questions.title: 包含动物的故事或书
questions.text: Many people regard pets as members of their family. What do you think?
questions.english: I can understand that view because people form routines and emotional connections with animals they care for. A pet may provide companionship and become part of everyday family life. However, treating it as family should also mean respecting its actual needs. Animals should not be expected to behave like people simply because their owners feel close to them.
questions.chinese: 我理解这种看法，因为人们会与自己照料的动物形成日常习惯和情感联系。宠物提供陪伴，成为家庭日常的一部分。但把它当家人也应尊重它真正的需求，不能因为亲近，就要求动物像人一样行为。

questions.title: 包含动物的故事或书
questions.text: Do many people keep pets in your country?
questions.english: Pet ownership is familiar in China, particularly with animals such as cats and dogs, but I would not estimate a national proportion. Whether someone keeps a pet depends on space, time, money and personal preference. Some people enjoy animals without owning one. I think responsible care matters more than whether keeping a pet is seen as fashionable or common.
questions.chinese: 养宠物在中国很常见，猫狗尤其为人熟悉，但我不会估计全国比例。是否养宠物取决于空间、时间、金钱和偏好。有些人喜欢动物，却不养。我认为负责任地照料，比养宠物是否流行或常见更重要。

questions.title: 包含动物的故事或书
questions.text: What are the advantages of keeping a pet?
questions.english: A pet can offer companionship and encourage a regular routine. Looking after it may also teach someone patience and responsibility. These benefits are not automatic, though, because caring for an animal takes time and money. People should choose a pet whose needs they can meet, rather than expect it to solve loneliness without any effort from them.
questions.chinese: 宠物能提供陪伴、促进规律作息，照料它也可能培养耐心和责任感。但好处不是自动发生，因为需要时间和金钱。人们应选择自己能满足其需求的宠物，而不是不付出努力就指望它解决孤独。

questions.title: 包含动物的故事或书
questions.text: Why do people always tell children stories with animals?
questions.english: Animals make stories easy for children to imagine and remember. Different characters can represent feelings or behaviours without making the lesson feel too direct. A story about a helpful rabbit, for example, can introduce kindness. However, children should eventually learn that real animals have their own needs and do not behave exactly like the human characters in stories.
questions.chinese: 动物使故事更容易让孩子想象和记住。不同角色可以表现情感或行为，又不让道理显得太直接。例如，热心兔子的故事能引出善良。不过，孩子最终也应了解真实动物有自身需求，并不完全像故事里的人格化角色。

questions.title: 保护环境的法律
questions.text:
Describe a law on environmental protection
You should say:
What it is
How you first learned about it
Who benefits from it
And explain how you feel about this law
questions.english:
A law on environmental protection I'd like to discuss is China's law aimed at preventing and controlling air pollution. In broad terms, it creates responsibilities for controlling emissions and protecting the quality of the air people breathe.

The first time I paid attention to it was through a news report explaining how pollution affects ordinary life. That made the idea of environmental law feel practical rather than distant. I realised that cleaner air depends not only on individual choices, but also on rules for businesses and public authorities.

The people who benefit include local residents, workers and anyone spending time outdoors. Children and people who are more sensitive to poor air quality may especially need that protection. Businesses can also benefit from clearer expectations when the rules are applied fairly.

I support the purpose of the law, but I think implementation matters as much as the written words. Requirements need to be understandable, monitoring needs to be reliable, and responsibility should not fall only on individuals. For me, a good environmental law connects a clear public goal with practical steps that people and organisations can actually follow.
questions.chinese:
我想谈中国旨在防治空气污染的法律。大体而言，它规定了控制排放、保障人们呼吸到的空气质量的责任。

我最初留意它，是通过一篇解释污染如何影响日常生活的新闻。这让我觉得环境法律很实际，而非遥远的概念。我意识到，清洁空气不只依赖个人选择，也需要针对企业和公共部门的规则。

受益者包括居民、劳动者以及在户外活动的人。孩子和对空气质量更敏感的人尤其需要保护。公平实施时，明确要求也有益于企业。

我支持法律目的，但认为法律的落实与写在纸上的规定同样重要。要求要容易理解，监测要可靠，责任不应只落在个人身上。在我看来，好的环境法律把明确的公共目标与个人和组织真正能够执行的具体步骤联系起来。
pending: 首次通过新闻了解该法的个人经历和感受为候选，未确认；不编造条款、日期或处罚数额。

questions.title: 保护环境的法律
questions.text: What kinds of rules do schools in China have?
questions.english: Schools in China commonly have rules about attendance, classroom behaviour, safety and academic honesty. Some also set expectations for uniforms or the use of phones. The details differ between schools. I think the strongest rules are those with a clear purpose, such as preventing bullying, and students should understand the reason rather than follow them only because punishment is possible.
questions.chinese: 中国学校通常有出勤、课堂行为、安全和学术诚信方面的规则，也有学校要求制服或规范手机使用。细节因学校而异。我认为最有力的规则都有明确目的，比如防止欺凌；学生应理解理由，而非仅因为可能受罚才遵守。

questions.title: 保护环境的法律
questions.text: Do you think school rules are important?
questions.english: Yes, sensible rules help students learn in a safe and predictable environment. Without them, disruption or bullying may make school unfair for others. However, importance does not mean every existing rule is good. Schools should review rules that create unnecessary restrictions and explain the useful ones, so discipline supports learning rather than becomes an end in itself.
questions.chinese: 重要。合理规则有助于在安全、可预测的环境中学习。缺少规则，干扰或欺凌可能让学校对他人不公平。不过，重要不意味着所有现行规则都好。学校应检查不必要的限制，解释有用规定，让纪律服务学习，而非成为目的本身。

questions.title: 保护环境的法律
questions.text: Are children unhappy with the school rules?
questions.english: Some children dislike rules when they feel the restrictions are unfair or the reasons are unclear. Others may accept them once they understand how they protect everyone. Children are also sensitive to inconsistency, especially if adults ignore the same standards. I think discussing the purpose and listening to concerns can reduce frustration without removing all expectations.
questions.chinese: 有些孩子觉得限制不公平、理由不清楚，就会不喜欢。另一些人理解规则如何保护大家后可能接受。孩子也对不一致敏感，成人无视同样标准时尤其如此。我认为讨论目的、倾听顾虑，可以减少不满，同时保留必要要求。

questions.title: 保护环境的法律
questions.text: How can parents and teachers help children understand and follow rules?
questions.english: They can explain the rule through simple examples and show what responsible behaviour looks like. Adults should follow the same principles themselves and apply consequences consistently. It also helps to let children ask questions. When a child breaks a rule, discussing the effect on others may teach more than simply telling them that they have been bad.
questions.chinese: 可以通过简单例子解释规则，并展示负责任的行为。成年人自己应遵循同样原则，保持后果处理一致，也应允许孩子提问。孩子违规时，讨论对他人的影响，可能比只说他们表现不好更有教育意义。

questions.title: 保护环境的法律
questions.text: What are the rules people should obey at work?
questions.english: At work, people should follow safety procedures, protect confidential information and treat colleagues respectfully. They also need to meet reasonable commitments and be honest about their work. The exact rules depend on the role. A laboratory and a shop have different risks, but clear expectations and fair treatment are useful in both, rather than relying on guesswork.
questions.chinese: 工作中应遵守安全程序、保护机密信息、尊重同事，也要履行合理承诺、诚实对待工作。具体规定依岗位而异。实验室和商店的风险不同，但明确要求和公平待遇对两者都有用，不能靠猜。

questions.title: 保护环境的法律
questions.text: What is the purpose of punishment?
questions.english: Punishment should discourage harmful behaviour, protect others and help the person understand what needs to change. It should be proportionate and fair rather than simply painful. In a school, a consequence can be combined with an explanation and a chance to repair harm. I think prevention and learning are better goals than revenge or public humiliation.
questions.chinese: 惩罚应阻止有害行为、保护他人，帮助当事人理解需要改什么。惩罚应适度公平，而非单纯让人痛苦。在学校，后果可以结合解释和弥补伤害的机会。我认为预防和学习，比报复或公开羞辱更好的目标。

questions.title: 很久没收到回复的信息
questions.text:
Describe a time when you sent a message or an email to someone but received no
reply for a long time
You should say:
Who you sent it to
What the message/email was about
Whether you finally received the reply
And explain how you felt about the experience
questions.english:
An occasion when I waited a long time for an email reply involved a conference organiser. I had sent a question about a practical arrangement for an academic event, because I wanted to know what I needed to prepare before travelling.

The message was quite short. I explained the issue, gave the relevant details and asked for clarification. I expected an answer within a few days, but almost a week passed without one. That was frustrating because I could not finish that part of my planning confidently.

At first, I kept checking my inbox, which did not help. I then looked through the event information again to make sure the answer was not already available. After that, I sent one polite follow-up instead of several repeated messages.

Eventually, I received a reply with the information I needed. The organiser explained that they had been dealing with many requests. I felt relieved, and the delay became easier to understand. The experience reminded me to leave extra time for communication and not assume that a slow answer means someone is deliberately ignoring me.
questions.chinese:
一次长时间等邮件回复的经历，与会议组织者有关。我询问学术活动的实际安排，因为想知道出行前需要准备什么。

消息很短，我说明问题、给相关信息并请求澄清。原以为几天内有答复，却快一周没有消息，令人烦躁，因为无法放心完成那部分规划。

开始我反复查收件箱，并没有帮助。后来又看了活动信息，确认其中还没有现成的答案。之后只礼貌跟进一次，而非连续催促。

最终，我收到了需要的信息。组织者解释说正在处理很多请求，我松了一口气，也更能理解这次延迟。这段经历提醒我，应给沟通留出额外时间，不要把慢回复自动当作故意忽视。
pending: 发给组织者的邮件、等待时长、跟进过程及对方解释均为候选故事；仅赴学术会议的背景已确认。

questions.title: 很久没收到回复的信息
questions.text: In what situations do people spend a long time responding to others’ messages?
questions.english: People may reply slowly when they are working, travelling or dealing with something urgent. A message may also need a careful answer rather than a quick response. Sometimes notifications are missed altogether. I would not automatically interpret a delay as disrespect, because the sender can see only the waiting time, not everything happening in the other person's life.
questions.chinese: 人们工作、旅行或处理急事时可能回复慢。有些消息需要认真回答，不能匆忙回复；有时通知干脆被漏看。我不会自动把延迟理解为不尊重，因为发信者只看见等了多久，看不见对方生活里的全部情况。

questions.title: 很久没收到回复的信息
questions.text: In what situations do people not respond to messages at all?
questions.english: Some messages are spam or irrelevant, so people reasonably choose not to answer. Other messages may feel intrusive, upsetting or difficult to respond to. Forgetfulness can also play a part. If there is an existing commitment, though, a short explanation is usually more considerate than silence, because it tells the other person what to expect.
questions.chinese: 有些消息是垃圾信息或无关内容，人们不回复很合理。另一些可能侵犯边界、令人不快或难以回应，也可能只是忘记了。但如果已有承诺，简短解释通常比沉默体贴，因为能让对方知道接下来如何预期。

questions.title: 很久没收到回复的信息
questions.text: What would you do if you did not receive a reply after sending out a message?
questions.english: I would first consider whether the message is urgent and whether I have allowed a reasonable amount of time. If it matters, I would send one polite follow-up or use another appropriate channel. Repeated messages may create pressure without helping. For something less important, I would wait and avoid assuming that the person is deliberately ignoring me.
questions.chinese: 我会先看消息是否紧急、是否已经给了合理时间。如果重要，会礼貌跟进一次，或使用另一个合适渠道。反复发消息可能只制造压力。对不那么重要的事，我会等待，避免认定对方故意不理我。

questions.title: 很久没收到回复的信息
questions.text: Why do some people prefer sending a message instead of making a call?
questions.english: Messages let people respond when they are available, rather than interrupting them immediately. They also provide a written record of details, which is useful for dates or instructions. Some people find it easier to organise their thoughts in writing. However, a call may be better for something urgent or emotionally complicated, where tone and immediate questions matter.
questions.chinese: 消息让人有空时回复，不会立刻打断，也保留细节的文字记录，适合日期或说明。有些人写下来更容易组织想法。不过，紧急或情感复杂的事情可能更适合电话，因为语气和即时提问很重要。

questions.title: 很久没收到回复的信息
questions.text: How do you show your respect in your messages?
questions.english: I would use a polite greeting when appropriate, explain my purpose clearly and avoid demanding an immediate reply. I would also consider the other person's time, especially when sending a long request. Saying thank you matters, but respect is not only about formal words. A concise message with enough context can be more considerate than an elaborate one.
questions.chinese: 合适时我会礼貌问候，清楚说明目的，避免要求立即回复。发长请求时，也会考虑对方时间。感谢重要，但尊重不只在于正式措辞。有充分背景的简洁消息，可能比冗长华丽的消息更体贴。

questions.title: 很久没收到回复的信息
questions.text: Why do some people feel angry when others don’t reply to their message?
questions.english: A delayed reply can make people feel ignored, especially if the message is important or they expect a quick answer. They may also interpret silence through their own worries. However, those feelings do not prove that the other person intended disrespect. Clear expectations about urgency and communication can help, rather than treating every delay as a personal rejection.
questions.chinese: 回复延迟会让人觉得被忽视，消息重要或预期快速回应时尤其如此。人们也可能带着自身焦虑解读沉默，但感受不证明对方有意不尊重。说明紧急程度和沟通预期更有帮助，而不是把每次延迟都当成拒绝。

questions.title: 长久目标/抱负
questions.text:
Describe a long-term goal/ambition you would like to achieve
You should say:
How long you have had this goal/ambition
What it is
How you will achieve it
And explain why you set it
questions.english:
My long-term ambition is to pursue a PhD abroad and continue doing research in embodied artificial intelligence. I've been planning this for about a year. I'm currently a master's student studying AI, with a particular focus on robotics, so this goal is closely connected with what I'm studying now.

The reason I want to study abroad is to broaden my horizons and experience a wider range of educational approaches. I hope that learning in a different environment will give me more ways to think about research problems.

In terms of the research itself, I'd like to work on bringing general-purpose intelligent robots into real-world use. Put simply, I want to help make robots that can deal with a wider range of tasks in practical settings. That's the direction I hope to explore more deeply.

To move towards this goal, I'm preparing for IELTS and working on my English. One possible next step would be to look for PhD programmes and supervisors whose research fits my interests. There is still a lot to prepare, but the goal gives my current studies and English preparation a clear direction.
questions.chinese:
我的长期目标是到海外读博士，继续研究具身人工智能。我已经规划了约一年。目前是人工智能专业硕士生，尤其关注机器人，因此这个目标与现有学习紧密相关。

想出国学习，是为了拓宽眼界、体验更多元的教育方式。我希望不同环境的学习能带来思考研究问题的更多方法。

研究方面，我想推动通用智能机器人进入实际应用。简单说，就是帮助机器人在现实场景处理更广泛的任务，这是希望继续深入探索的方向。

为实现目标，我正在准备雅思、提高英语。一个可能的下一步是寻找研究兴趣匹配的博士项目和导师。还有许多要准备，但这个目标让当前学习和英语备考有明确方向。

questions.title: 长久目标/抱负
questions.text: Why should children have ambitions?
questions.english: Ambitions can give children a reason to explore interests and practise new skills. A goal also helps them see that effort can lead to progress. However, the ambition should not become a source of constant pressure. Children need room to change their minds, and adults should value curiosity and improvement rather than only a prestigious future job.
questions.chinese: 抱负让孩子有理由探索兴趣、练新技能，也帮助看见努力带来进步。但目标不应变成持续压力。孩子需要改变主意的空间，成年人应重视好奇心和进步，而非只盯着未来体面的职业。

questions.title: 长久目标/抱负
questions.text: What do you think of people going after high positions?
questions.english: Seeking a higher position can be reasonable if someone wants more responsibility and the chance to contribute. It can motivate them to develop their skills. The problem is when status becomes more important than competence or fair treatment. I would respect ambition that is supported by good work, rather than promotion pursued at the expense of colleagues.
questions.chinese: 希望升到更高职位是合理的，尤其是想承担责任、增加贡献时，也能激励提升能力。问题在于地位超过了能力或公平待遇。我尊重靠好工作支持的抱负，而非牺牲同事来争取晋升。

questions.title: 长久目标/抱负
questions.text: Why are some young people keen on being fans of superstars?
questions.english: Superstars can offer excitement, a sense of identity and a community of other fans. Young people may admire their talent or feel inspired by their achievements. Following someone also creates topics to share with friends. However, enthusiasm needs limits; it should not replace study, relationships or financial judgement, especially when advertising encourages fans to spend more.
questions.chinese: 巨星可以带来兴奋感、认同感和粉丝社群。年轻人可能欣赏才华，或受成就鼓舞，关注名人也提供与朋友分享的话题。但热情需要限度，尤其在广告鼓励消费时，不应替代学习、人际关系或财务判断。

questions.title: 长久目标/抱负
questions.text: Is it good for a person to be ambitious?
questions.english: Ambition can be positive because it encourages people to set goals and persist through difficulties. It becomes less helpful when the goal is unrealistic or success is defined only by status. I think healthy ambition combines effort with flexibility. Someone should be able to learn from setbacks and adjust the route without feeling that their entire worth has disappeared.
questions.chinese: 抱负积极的一面是让人设目标、坚持克服困难。目标不现实或只用地位定义成功时，就不太有帮助。我认为健康抱负结合努力与弹性：遇挫能学习、调整路线，不觉得自己的全部价值消失了。

questions.title: 长久目标/抱负
questions.text: Do you think it is necessary to be ambitious when working in a team in a company?
questions.english: Some ambition is useful because team members need motivation to improve and contribute. However, personal goals should be compatible with the group's purpose. If everyone only competes for recognition, cooperation suffers. I would value people who want to develop their own skills while helping the team succeed, rather than treating colleagues as obstacles to their next promotion.
questions.chinese: 适度抱负有用，因为成员需要动力去改进、贡献。但个人目标应与团队目的相容。如果人人只争认可，合作会受损。我重视既发展自身技能、也帮助团队成功的人，而非把同事当晋升障碍。

questions.title: 长久目标/抱负
questions.text: Should parents support their children in pursuing their ambitions?
questions.english: Parents should take children's ambitions seriously and help them explore what the goal involves. Support may mean information, encouragement or opportunities to practise, rather than agreeing to every request. If a goal is unrealistic, a respectful conversation is better than dismissal. Children should learn to compare options and revise plans while knowing that their interests still matter.
questions.chinese: 家长应认真对待孩子的抱负，帮助了解目标涉及什么。支持可能是信息、鼓励或练习机会，而非答应所有要求。目标不现实时，尊重地交流比否定更好。孩子应学会比较选项、调整计划，同时知道自己的兴趣仍被重视。

questions.title: 改变重要想法
questions.text:
Describe a time when you changed an important opinion of yours
You should say:
When you changed your opinion
What the original opinion was
Why you changed it
And explain how you felt about the experience
questions.english:
An important opinion I changed was the idea that an impressive demonstration is enough to show that an AI system is useful. Earlier this year, while thinking more carefully about robotics, I began to see the limits of that view.

Originally, I was strongly attracted to a system that could complete a task in a short video. If the result looked smooth, it was easy to assume that the underlying technology was ready for practical use. But a demonstration may show only the best attempt under carefully selected conditions.

What changed my mind was considering how the same system would behave when the situation was slightly different. A robot might face an unfamiliar object, poor lighting or a person moving unexpectedly. Those conditions reveal whether it can actually cope, rather than simply repeat a successful example.

I now think reliability, testing and clear limits matter as much as an attractive demonstration. I felt that the new view was less exciting at first, but more realistic. It did not make me less interested in AI. Instead, it made the questions I wanted to ask more useful: not just whether something can work once, but whether people can depend on it.
questions.chinese:
我改变的一个重要观点，是认为令人印象深刻的演示足以证明AI有用。今年较早时，更认真思考机器人后，我开始看到这种想法的局限。

原先，我很容易被短视频中成功完成任务的系统吸引。如果结果流畅，就容易以为技术已可实际使用。但演示可能只展示精心挑选的条件下表现最好的一次尝试。

改变想法的是思考同一系统在情境略有变化时会怎样。机器人可能遇到陌生物体、光线不好，或有人突然移动。这些情况才说明它能否应对，而非只重复成功例子。

现在我认为可靠性、测试和明确局限，与漂亮演示同样重要。起初新观点没那么令人兴奋，却更现实，也没让我失去AI兴趣，反而让问题更有用：不只看能否成功一次，而是看人们能否依赖它。
pending: 旧观点、观点改变时间和思考过程为候选成长故事，尚未确认，不作为用户真实研究记录。

questions.title: 改变重要想法
questions.text: When do most children begin to have their own opinions?
questions.english: Children begin expressing preferences quite early, but forming a reasoned opinion develops gradually. As they gain language, experience and opportunities to ask questions, they can explain why they think something. I would not give one exact age for everyone. Adults can support the process by listening and asking simple follow-up questions instead of immediately correcting every different view.
questions.chinese: 孩子很早就表达偏好，但有理由的观点是逐渐形成的。语言、经验和提问机会增加后，就能解释为什么这样想。我不会给所有人规定一个精确年龄。成年人可以倾听、简单追问，而不是立即纠正每一种不同看法。

questions.title: 改变重要想法
questions.text: Whose opinions are more important to children, their parents' or teachers'?
questions.english: Both can be important, but in different areas. Parents know a child's daily life and values, while teachers may offer more experience with learning and school behaviour. Neither should automatically overrule the other on every issue. I think children benefit when adults explain their reasons and help them consider different views, rather than ask them to choose one authority blindly.
questions.chinese: 两者都重要，但领域不同。父母了解孩子的日常和价值观，老师则更熟悉学习和校园行为。不应在每个问题上自动让一方压过另一方。成年人解释理由、帮助考虑不同看法，比要求孩子盲选一个权威更有益。

questions.title: 改变重要想法
questions.text: Do children communicate more with teachers or with parents?
questions.english: It depends on the child, the relationship and the topic. A child may discuss schoolwork with a teacher but share personal worries with a parent, or the reverse if one relationship feels safer. Time together also matters. I think the important question is whether the child has someone trustworthy to talk to, rather than which adult receives more conversations.
questions.chinese: 取决于孩子、关系和话题。孩子可能与老师谈功课、与家长谈烦恼；如果另一段关系更安全，也可能相反。相处时间也重要。我认为关键是有没有可信的人可倾诉，而非哪位成年人获得更多谈话。

questions.title: 改变重要想法
questions.text: Who do young people like to share opinions with?
questions.english: Young people may share opinions with friends who understand their interests, but they can also turn to parents, teachers or online communities. The choice depends on trust and the subject being discussed. Someone may want practical advice in one situation and emotional support in another. I think a good listener matters more than belonging to a particular age group.
questions.chinese: 年轻人可能与理解自身兴趣的朋友交流，也会找父母、老师或网上社群。选择取决于信任和话题。有时想要实际建议，有时需要情感支持。我认为愿意好好倾听，比属于某个特定年龄群体更重要。

questions.title: 想要颁布的环保法律
questions.text:
Describe an environmental law you would like your country to introduce
You should say:
What law it should be
Why people should follow the law
Whether the law will be popular
And explain how you feel about this law
questions.english:
An environmental law I would like to see introduced is a requirement for electronic products to carry clear information about how repairable they are. Manufacturers would need to explain whether common parts can be replaced and how long suitable spare parts will be available.

The reason is that a small fault can sometimes lead people to replace an entire device. If they knew a repair was possible and affordable, they might keep it longer. That could reduce waste and the resources needed to produce a new product. Shops and manufacturers would need to follow the rule so consumers could compare information fairly.

I think the law could be popular with people who want to avoid unnecessary spending. Some companies might object because providing parts and clear information takes effort. So the requirement would need a practical timetable and consistent standards rather than a vague promise.

I would feel positive about it because it connects environmental protection with an everyday decision. It would not force everyone to keep a broken device forever, but it would give them a realistic choice before buying something new. That seems more helpful than simply telling people to consume less.
questions.chinese:
我希望推出一条环保法规，要求电子产品清楚标明可维修程度。制造商需要说明常见零件能否更换，以及合适的备件能供应多久。

原因是，一个小故障有时就会让人更换整台设备。如果知道能够维修，而且费用合理，人们就可能使用更久，从而减少废弃物，以及生产新产品所需的资源。商店和制造商都需要遵守这条规定，让消费者能够公平地比较这些信息。

我认为，希望避免不必要支出的人会欢迎这条法规。不过，有些公司可能会反对，因为供应配件和提供清楚的信息都需要投入。因此，这项要求需要切实可行的时间表和统一的标准，而不是一个模糊的承诺。

我会支持这条法规，因为它把环保与日常生活中的决定联系起来。它不会强迫每个人永远留着坏掉的设备，而是在购买新产品前，给人们一个可行的选择。这似乎比单纯劝人少消费更有帮助。

questions.title: 想要颁布的环保法律
questions.text: How does technology affect the law?
questions.english: Technology creates new activities that laws may need to address, such as handling personal data or deciding responsibility for automated systems. It can also help officials detect problems and make services easier to access. However, rules should not be rushed simply because a tool is new. They need clear principles that protect people while allowing useful innovation.
questions.chinese: 技术带来法律可能需要处理的新活动，比如个人数据管理、自动化系统责任认定，也能帮助部门发现问题、提升服务可及性。不过，不能只因工具新就仓促立规，应有清晰原则，在保护人们的同时允许有用创新。

questions.title: 想要颁布的环保法律
questions.text: What kinds of rules do schools in China have?
questions.english: Schools in China commonly have rules about attendance, classroom behaviour, safety and academic honesty. Some also set expectations for uniforms or the use of phones. The details differ between schools. I think the strongest rules are those with a clear purpose, such as preventing bullying, and students should understand the reason rather than follow them only because punishment is possible.
questions.chinese: 中国学校通常有出勤、课堂行为、安全和学术诚信方面的规则，也有学校要求制服或规范手机使用。细节因学校而异。我认为最有力的规则都有明确目的，比如防止欺凌；学生应理解理由，而非仅因为可能受罚才遵守。

questions.title: 想要颁布的环保法律
questions.text: Will there be a law that is universally accepted?
questions.english: A broad principle, such as protecting people from serious harm, might receive very wide support. However, agreeing on the exact wording and enforcement is much harder. Countries differ in legal traditions, resources and priorities. I think common ground is possible, but a law accepted without disagreement by absolutely everyone would be difficult to achieve in practice.
questions.chinese: 保护人们免受严重伤害这样的广泛原则，可能得到很大支持，但具体措辞和执法更难达成一致。各国法律传统、资源和重点不同。我认为可以找到共同点，但实际中很难有一部所有人都毫无异议接受的法律。

questions.title: 想要颁布的环保法律
questions.text: What environmental laws does your country already have?
questions.english: China has environmental laws covering issues such as air pollution, water pollution and the protection of natural resources. Waste management also involves legal responsibilities and local rules. I would not claim to know every detailed provision. What matters to ordinary people is understanding the requirements relevant to their lives and seeing that businesses and individuals follow them fairly.
questions.chinese: 中国的环境法律涉及空气污染、水污染、自然资源保护等问题。废物管理也包括法律责任和地方规则。我不会说自己知道每项具体条文。对普通人而言，重要的是理解与生活有关的要求，并看到企业和个人公平遵守。

questions.title: 当地新闻
questions.text:
Describe a piece of local news that people are interested in
You should say:
What it was about
Where you saw/heard it
Who was involved
And explain why people were interested in it
questions.english:
A piece of local news that could attract a lot of interest was an announcement that a public library would extend its evening opening hours. The report explained that a study area would stay available later, giving residents more flexibility after work or classes.

I saw the announcement in a local online news article. It involved the library staff, the local authorities supporting the service and residents who wanted a quiet place to read or study. The report also described practical details, such as which area would be open and how visitors could use it.

I think people were interested because the change affected ordinary life directly. Not everyone has a quiet home environment, and some people finish work too late to use a library during normal daytime hours. A relatively small change in a public service could therefore create a useful opportunity.

What made the story appealing to me was its practical scale. It was not about a dramatic event or a famous person. It was about making an existing resource more accessible. As a student, I can understand why a reliable, calm place to study would matter to people.
questions.chinese:
可能吸引许多人关注的一则本地新闻，是公共图书馆宣布延长晚间开放时间。报道解释部分学习区域会开放更晚，让居民下班或下课后更灵活使用。

我在一篇本地网络新闻报道中看到了这则公告，涉及图书馆工作人员、支持服务的地方部门，以及想找安静地方阅读学习的居民。报道也有具体信息，比如开放哪一区、如何使用。

我认为人们关注，是因为变化直接影响日常。不是人人家里安静，有些人下班太晚，无法在白天正常时段去图书馆。所以公共服务的小变化也能带来有用机会。

吸引我的是，这则新闻着眼于日常生活中的具体问题：不是戏剧事件或名人，而是让已有资源更易获得。作为学生，我理解可靠安静的学习空间为什么重要。
pending: 图书馆公告、网络文章及具体服务变化均为未确认候选新闻，不声称已联网核验或已在用户城市发生。

questions.title: 当地新闻
questions.text: Do people read the newspaper where you live?
questions.english: I would expect some people still to read printed newspapers, while others prefer news on their phones. Print can offer a regular reading routine, but digital news is easier to access and update. Age and personal habits probably influence the choice. I would not describe everyone in my area the same way, because news habits vary considerably.
questions.chinese: 我想仍有人读纸报，也有人偏好手机新闻。纸报能提供规律阅读习惯，数字新闻则更易获取和更新。年龄和个人习惯可能影响选择。我不会把居住地区所有人都说成一样，因为新闻习惯差异很大。
pending: 居住地区实际读报情况未提供；此稿使用预期表达，未声称调查结果。

questions.title: 当地新闻
questions.text: Do people prefer local or international news?
questions.english: Local news is useful when it concerns transport, services or decisions affecting daily life. International news helps people understand events with wider consequences. I think many readers need a mixture rather than one category only. Their priorities may change with the situation: a local weather warning can be urgent even for someone who usually follows global affairs.
questions.chinese: 地方新闻涉及交通、服务或日常决策时很有用；国际新闻帮助理解影响更广的事件。我认为许多人需要两者结合，而非只选一类。重点随情境变化：即使平时关注全球事务，地方天气预警也可能更紧急。

questions.title: 当地新闻
questions.text: Do you think it's important to have a national identity?
questions.english: A national identity can give people a sense of belonging and a connection with shared history or culture. It may also encourage responsibility towards the community. However, it should not require looking down on other countries. I think a healthy identity allows pride and criticism together, while respecting people whose backgrounds or opinions are different.
questions.chinese: 民族或国家认同能带来归属感，让人连接共同历史和文化，也可能促进社区责任。但不应要求轻视别国。我认为健康认同应允许自豪与批评并存，同时尊重背景或观点不同的人。

questions.title: 当地新闻
questions.text: How can people develop their national identity?
questions.english: People can learn about their country's history, languages, arts and everyday traditions. Taking part in community activities can also make identity feel connected with real people rather than only symbols. Education should show both achievements and difficult experiences honestly. I think an informed understanding creates a stronger identity than repeating slogans without knowing what they mean.
questions.chinese: 人们可以了解本国历史、语言、艺术和日常传统，参加社区活动也能让认同连接真实的人，而非只有符号。教育应诚实呈现成就与艰难经历。我认为有知识基础的理解，比不懂意思地重复口号更能建立稳固认同。

questions.title: 近期改变
questions.text:
Describe a change that you made recently
You should say:
What the change was
What caused the change
What you did for the change
And explain how you feel about the change
questions.english:
A recent change I'd describe is keeping my phone out of reach during a focused study session. Previously, I would leave it beside my laptop, so even a small notification could interrupt what I was doing.

The reason for changing was that I wanted my English preparation to be more deliberate. Simply sitting at the desk for a long time did not guarantee useful work. If I checked messages repeatedly, it became harder to follow a difficult sentence or stay with a task that needed concentration.

I started by switching off unnecessary notifications and leaving the phone away from the desk. I also gave each study session a small, clear goal and checked the phone during a planned break. At first, the habit felt slightly uncomfortable because reaching for it was almost automatic.

What I like about the change is that it is simple. It does not require a complicated application or a perfect timetable. It just removes one source of distraction. I would describe the feeling as calmer and more purposeful: I can judge a session by what I understood or completed, rather than only by how long I was sitting there.
questions.chinese:
我想描述的近期变化，是专注学习时把手机放到够不到的位置。原先放在笔记本旁，小通知也会打断。

改变是为了让英语备考更有目的。在书桌前坐很久，并不保证学习有效；反复查消息会让理解难句、专注任务更困难。

我先关掉不必要通知，把手机放离桌面；再给每段学习设小而清晰的目标，在计划好的休息时看手机。最初略不习惯，因为伸手拿手机几乎成了下意识的动作。

我喜欢它的简单：无需复杂软件或完美时间表，只减少一个干扰来源。我会把感觉描述为更平静、更有目标；可以用真正理解或完成了什么评价学习，而不只计算坐了多久。
pending: 手机原习惯、实际改变、执行步骤和效果均为完整候选，不视为用户已实施学习改进。

questions.title: 近期改变
questions.text: Do you think it is good to change one’s daily routine?
questions.english: Changing a routine can be useful if the current one no longer fits someone's needs. It may create time for exercise, study or proper rest. However, frequent changes without a reason can make healthy habits harder to maintain. I would try a small adjustment, observe whether it helps and keep the parts that already work well.
questions.chinese: 现有作息不再适合需求时，改变可能有用，能为运动、学习或充分休息腾时间。但无理由地频繁改变，会让好习惯难维持。我会小幅调整，观察效果，并保留已有效的部分。

questions.title: 近期改变
questions.text: Do you think it is good to change jobs?
questions.english: Changing jobs can be a good decision when it offers better learning, fairer conditions or work that fits someone's goals. It can also involve uncertainty and the cost of starting again. I would compare the reasons carefully rather than move only because of a temporary frustration. Staying or leaving should depend on the long-term situation, not one difficult day.
questions.chinese: 换工作能带来更好的学习机会、更公平的条件，或更符合目标的工作时，可以是好决定，但也有不确定性和重新开始的成本。我会认真比较原因，不只因短暂挫败离开。去留应看长期情况，而非某个困难日子。

questions.title: 近期改变
questions.text: Is it good for people to get a job promotion?
questions.english: A promotion can recognise good work and give someone more influence, responsibility or income. Those benefits can be valuable, but the new role may also bring stress or less time for technical work. I think a promotion is positive when the person understands the role and genuinely wants it, rather than accepts it only because a higher title looks impressive.
questions.chinese: 晋升能认可工作，带来更多影响力、责任或收入，这些很有价值，但也可能增加压力、减少技术工作时间。我认为在理解岗位、真正想承担时，晋升才积极，而非只因更高头衔好看就接受。

questions.title: 近期改变
questions.text: Do people often make plans around their regular routines?
questions.english: Yes, regular routines often provide the starting point for a plan. People arrange errands, meetings or study around fixed commitments such as work and meals. That makes time easier to estimate. However, a routine should not prevent useful changes. If the same schedule repeatedly leaves something important unfinished, it may be better to adjust the routine itself.
questions.chinese: 会，固定作息常是计划的起点。人们围绕工作、吃饭等固定安排组织办事、会面或学习，让时间更易估算。但作息不应阻止有用改变。如果同样日程反复让重要事项未完成，可能应调整作息本身。

questions.title: 近期改变
questions.text: Who tend to change their daily routine more, young people or old people?
questions.english: Young people may experience more changes because education, work and living arrangements are still developing. Older people may have more established habits, but health, retirement or family needs can also change their routines. I would not make age the only explanation. The amount of control someone has over their time can matter just as much.
questions.chinese: 年轻人可能变化更多，因为学业、工作和居住安排仍在发展。年长者习惯可能更稳定，但健康、退休或家庭需要也会改变作息。我不会只用年龄解释，个人对时间有多少控制权，同样重要。

questions.title: Lost and found
questions.text: Have you ever lost your keys?
questions.english: Yes, I once misplaced them in a bag and spent a while searching. They hadn't actually been stolen or left outside; I'd just put them in an unusual pocket.
questions.chinese: 丢过，我曾把钥匙放错在包里，找了一阵。它们没被偷也没落在外面，只是放到了不常用的口袋。

questions.title: Lost and found

questions.chinese: 如果东西可能在附近被找到，我会发帖。我会少公开个人信息，也会联系最后记得拿着它的那个地方。

questions.title: Lost and found
questions.text: Have you ever lost things?
questions.english: Yes, I've misplaced small things, such as keys, rather than anything very valuable. Usually I'd retrace my steps and check the places where I last used them.
questions.chinese: 丢过，我放错过钥匙这类小东西，而不是特别贵重的物品。我通常会回想之前走过的地方，并查看最后用它们的位置。

questions.title: Lost and found

questions.chinese: 如果物品贵重或里面有身份证明，我会联系警察或相关工作人员。这比完全靠自己寻找失主更稳妥。

questions.title: Lost and found
questions.text: What will you do if you find something lost by others?
questions.english: I'd first look for an obvious way to identify the owner. If that wasn't possible, I'd hand it to staff or the police rather than take it home.
questions.chinese: 我会先看看有没有明显方式识别失主。如果没有，就交给工作人员或警察，而不是带回家。

questions.title: Computers/tablets
questions.text: Would you like to use a computer or tablet?
questions.english: I'd choose a computer, especially for programming. A tablet could be useful for reading, but a keyboard and a larger working space would suit my main interests better.
questions.chinese: 我会选电脑，尤其为了编程。平板可能适合阅读，但键盘和更大的操作空间更符合我的主要兴趣。
pending: 编程阅读爱好真实；电脑相对平板的选择为候选。

questions.title: Computers/tablets
questions.text: In what conditions would you use a computer or tablet?
questions.english: I'd use a computer for programming or other tasks that need detailed input. For relaxed reading, a tablet could be convenient because it's easier to hold and move around.
questions.chinese: 我会用电脑编程或做其他需要细致输入的任务。轻松阅读时，平板可能方便，因为更容易拿着和移动。
pending: 编程阅读爱好真实；设备选择情境为候选，不声称拥有平板。

questions.title: Computers/tablets
questions.text: When was the first time you used a computer or tablet?
questions.english: I first used a computer at school when I was younger. I mainly explored basic functions then, so it was quite different from the programming I'm interested in now.
questions.chinese: 我小时候第一次在学校用电脑。那时主要探索基本功能，和现在感兴趣的编程很不一样。

questions.title: Computers/tablets
questions.text: What would your life be like without computers or tablets?
questions.english: It would be much harder to pursue my interests in programming and AI. I'd still have books and other activities, but losing access to computers would affect a central part of my life.
questions.chinese: 那会让编程和AI兴趣更难实现。我仍可以看书、做其他活动，但无法用电脑会影响生活的重要部分。

questions.title: Computers/tablets
questions.text: In what conditions would it be difficult for you to use a computer or tablet?
questions.english: I'd struggle without reliable electricity or a comfortable place to work. A noisy setting could also make complicated tasks difficult, even if the computer itself worked perfectly.
questions.chinese: 没有可靠电力或舒服的工作位置时，我会很难使用。嘈杂环境也会让复杂任务困难，即使电脑本身运转正常。

questions.title: Collecting things
questions.text: Do you collect things?
questions.english: I'd be more interested in keeping useful books than collecting expensive objects. I enjoy reading, so a small collection that I actually use would appeal to me.
questions.chinese: 比起收集贵重物品，我更有兴趣保存有用的书。我喜欢阅读，所以真正会使用的小书藏会吸引我。

questions.title: Collecting things

questions.chinese: 我会把日常用品放在几个固定位置，书放在阅读处附近。这样不用复杂收纳系统，也能方便找到东西。
pending: 该偏好或习惯为完整候选，待确认是否符合本人。

questions.title: Collecting things

questions.english: Yes, if they remained useful or had personal meaning. I'd be selective, though, because keeping everything would eventually make it difficult to organise the things I genuinely need.
questions.chinese: 会，如果它们仍有用或有个人意义。但我会有选择，因为什么都留着，最后会难以整理真正需要的东西。
pending: 该偏好或习惯为完整候选，待确认是否符合本人。

questions.title: Collecting things
questions.text: Are there any things you have kept from your childhood?
questions.english: I've kept a small school notebook because it reminds me of how I used to think. It isn't valuable financially, but looking through it can bring back memories.
questions.chinese: 我保留了一本学校时期的小笔记本，因为它让我想起以前怎样思考。它不值钱，但翻阅时能唤起回忆。

questions.title: Street market
questions.text: Are there many street markets in China?
questions.english: There are street markets in many parts of China, although their size and frequency vary. They're often places to buy food or everyday items rather than luxury products.
questions.chinese: 中国很多地方都有街市，不过规模和开放频率不同。人们通常在那里买食品或日用品，而不是奢侈品。

questions.title: Street market

questions.chinese: 上周末我去过一个小型本地市场看看水果。时间不长，但亲眼看摊位让挑选更方便。

questions.title: Feeling bored
questions.text: Do you think childhood is boring or adulthood is boring?
questions.english: Neither is automatically boring. Children may have fewer choices, while adults have more responsibilities. I'd say boredom depends more on curiosity and how people use their time.
questions.chinese: 两者都不一定无聊。儿童选择可能较少，成人责任更多。我觉得无聊更取决于好奇心和人们怎样使用时间。

questions.chinese: 我会根据精力选择读书、编程或日本动漫。几种兴趣给我多个选择，不必一直刷相同内容。
