questions.title: Feeling bored
questions.text: When would you feel bored?
questions.english: I'd feel bored when an activity became repetitive and had no clear purpose. Even a difficult task can hold my attention if I understand what I'm trying to achieve.
questions.chinese: 活动重复且没有明确目的时，我会无聊。只要明白想实现什么，即使困难任务也能吸引我的注意。
pending: 该偏好或习惯为完整候选，待确认是否符合本人。

questions.title: Feeling bored
questions.text: Do you often feel bored?
questions.english: Not often, because reading, programming and anime give me different things to do. Still, I'd probably feel bored if I spent too long doing one repetitive activity.
questions.chinese: 不经常，因为阅读、编程和动漫给我不同的事情做。不过，同一种重复活动做太久，我大概也会无聊。
pending: 爱好真实；无聊频率和触发条件为候选。

questions.title: Friends
questions.text: Would you invite friends to your home?
questions.english: Yes, if we arranged it beforehand and my mother was comfortable with it. I'd prefer a small visit where we could talk naturally rather than a noisy gathering.
questions.chinese: 会，如果事先安排好、母亲也觉得合适。我更喜欢能自然聊天的小聚，而不是吵闹聚会。
pending: 同住母亲和性格真实；邀请朋友及家庭安排为候选。

questions.title: Friends
questions.text: Do you prefer to spend time with one friend or with a group of friends?
questions.english: I'd usually choose one friend or a small group. I'm fairly quiet initially but talkative with familiar people, so a relaxed setting would make conversation easier.
questions.chinese: 我通常会选一个朋友或小群体。我起初安静，熟人面前健谈，所以轻松场合让聊天更容易。
pending: 性格真实；人数偏好为候选。

questions.title: Friends
questions.text: Do you have a friend you have known for a long time?
questions.english: Yes, I have a friend from school whom I've known for years. We don't need to talk constantly, but catching up still feels comfortable because we share that background.
questions.chinese: 有，我有一位认识多年的学校朋友。我们不需要不停联系，但因为有共同背景，聊近况仍然自在。
pending: 多年学校朋友、联系频率和共同背景为候选，不增入真实人物库。

questions.title: Friends
questions.text: What do you usually do with your friends?
questions.english: I'd usually chat, share recommendations or have something to eat together. Since I enjoy books and anime, those could give us easy topics without needing a complicated plan.
questions.chinese: 我通常会聊天、分享推荐，或一起吃东西。我喜欢书和动漫，这些能提供容易聊的话题，不需要复杂安排。
pending: 爱好真实；朋友活动与共同兴趣尚未确认。

questions.title: Friends
questions.text: Where do you often meet each other?
questions.english: I'd prefer a quiet café or somewhere with enough space to sit comfortably. Being able to hear each other would matter more than choosing the most fashionable place.
questions.chinese: 我更喜欢安静咖啡馆，或有足够空间舒服坐着的地方。能听清彼此，比选择最时髦的地方更重要。
pending: 该偏好或习惯为完整候选，待确认是否符合本人。

questions.title: Friends
questions.text: Do you often go out with your friends?
questions.english: Not constantly. I'd prefer occasional relaxed meetings rather than a busy social schedule. With close friends, though, I can be quite talkative once we start chatting.
questions.chinese: 不会一直出门。我更喜欢偶尔轻松见面，而不是密集社交。不过，和亲近朋友开始聊天后，我可以很健谈。
pending: 熟人面前健谈真实；聚会频率和社交安排为候选。

questions.title: Friends
questions.text: How important are friends to you?
questions.english: They'd be important because familiar people give me space to talk openly. I'd value a few genuine connections more than simply knowing a large number of people.
questions.chinese: 朋友很重要，因为熟人让我能敞开交流。比起只认识很多人，我更看重几段真诚关系。
pending: 该偏好或习惯为完整候选，待确认是否符合本人。

questions.title: Friends
questions.text: Why are some places suitable for meeting while others are not?
questions.english: Noise, seating and privacy make a difference. A place where people can hear each other and stay comfortably supports conversation, while a crowded, loud setting can make it tiring.
questions.chinese: 噪声、座位和私密性会产生影响。能听清彼此、舒服待着的地方有利于交流，拥挤吵闹环境则让人疲惫。
pending: 个人立场待确认。

questions.title: Friends
questions.text: Is there a difference between where you meet friends now and where you used to meet them in the past?
questions.english: At school, we often met in classrooms or nearby open spaces. Now I'd choose somewhere like a café, where we could sit down and talk without rushing to the next lesson.
questions.chinese: 在学校时，我们常在教室或附近空地见面。现在我会选咖啡馆这类能坐下聊天、不必赶着上下一节课的地方。
pending: 候选学校朋友见面场所与现在咖啡馆比较；并非已确认经历。

questions.title: 印象深刻的课程
questions.text:
Describe a course that impressed you a lot
You should say:
What the course was about
Where you took the course
What you did during the course
And explain why it impressed you a lot
questions.english:
A course that impressed me was an introductory robotics course at university. It explored how a robot senses its surroundings, makes a decision and turns that decision into movement. The combination of ideas was more interesting than looking at each part separately.

The course included classroom explanations and practical work in a computer lab. In one exercise, we wrote a small programme for a virtual robot to follow a path. We then changed conditions and checked whether the same method still worked. A solution that looked good in one test was not always reliable in another.

What I did was not just listen and copy notes. I had to describe the problem, try a method, examine the result and explain why it failed. Discussing different approaches also helped me see that a technical problem can have more than one reasonable solution.

The course impressed me because it connected theory with something observable. It made robotics feel like a field of real decisions and limitations rather than only exciting demonstrations. That connection is what I value in a good course: I should leave with better questions as well as more information.
questions.chinese:
让我印象深刻的是大学一门机器人入门课，研究机器人如何感知环境、决策，再将决策转化为动作。各部分结合起来，比单独看更有意思。

课程有课堂讲解和计算机实验室实践。一项练习是写小程序，让虚拟机器人沿路径走；再改变条件，检查方法是否仍有效。一种测试里表现好的方案，在另一种里未必可靠。

我不只听讲、抄笔记，还要描述问题、尝试方法、检查结果、解释失败。讨论不同方法，也让我看到技术问题可能不只有一种合理方案。

课程把理论与可观察的现象连接起来，令机器人领域呈现真实决策和局限，而不只有激动人心的演示。我重视这种联系：学完后，不仅应掌握更多信息，也应形成更有价值的问题。
pending: 具体课程、授课地点和虚拟机器人练习均为候选细节，未确认用户曾上过该课。

questions.title: 印象深刻的课程
questions.text: What can we learn from history?
questions.english: History helps us understand how present institutions, ideas and conflicts developed. It also gives examples of choices and their consequences. However, the past does not repeat in exactly the same conditions, so we should be cautious about simple lessons. I think studying evidence and different perspectives is valuable because it teaches people to question easy explanations.
questions.chinese: 历史帮助理解当前制度、思想和冲突如何形成，也展示选择及其后果。但过去不会在完全一样的条件下重演，因此应谨慎对待简单教训。我认为研究证据和不同视角很有价值，能教人质疑过于轻易的解释。

questions.title: 印象深刻的课程
questions.text: What do people need to remember in their daily lives?
questions.english: People need to remember appointments, responsibilities and important details about the people around them. Practical information, such as where they left something or when a task is due, also matters. They do not need to keep every detail in their head. A reliable reminder system can help them focus on understanding and decisions rather than constant worry about forgetting.
questions.chinese: 人们需记住预约、责任和身边人的重要信息，也需记东西放在哪里、任务何时到期等实用细节。但不必把一切装在脑中。可靠提醒系统让人更专注理解和决策，而不是一直担心忘事。

questions.title: 印象深刻的课程
questions.text: Can technology help people remember things better? How?
questions.english: Yes, calendars, notes and reminders can help people remember tasks and retrieve information when needed. Photos can also provide cues for an experience. However, storing something is not the same as learning it. For knowledge we need to use independently, active recall and practice still matter, so technology works best as support rather than a replacement for all memory.
questions.chinese: 可以，日历、笔记和提醒帮助记任务、必要时找信息，照片也能提供经历的线索。但保存不等于学会。需要独立运用的知识仍需主动回忆和练习，因此技术最好辅助记忆，而非完全代替它。

questions.title: 印象深刻的课程
questions.text: Which can help people remember things better, words or photos?
questions.english: Photos are often better for remembering a place, a face or the atmosphere of an event. Words can preserve explanations, names and details that a picture does not show. I would use both when the memory matters. A short caption beside a photo can connect the visual cue with the meaning, which makes later recall more complete.
questions.chinese: 照片常更适合记地点、面孔或活动氛围。文字能保存图片不显示的解释、名字和细节。重要记忆我会两者结合：照片旁的简短说明，把视觉线索与意义连接起来，让日后回忆更完整。

questions.title: 印象深刻的课程
questions.text: Do people like things of memorial significance?
questions.english: Yes, an ordinary object can feel valuable because it connects someone with a person or an important period of life. Its financial price may be quite low, but the memory gives it meaning. Not everyone expresses this by keeping many objects, though. Some prefer photos or stories, so sentimental value can be preserved in different ways.
questions.chinese: 会。普通物品因连接某个人或人生重要时期，也能很珍贵。价格可能很低，但记忆赋予意义。不过，并非人人都保存很多东西，也有人更喜欢照片或故事，因此纪念价值可以通过不同方式保留。

questions.title: 印象深刻的课程
questions.text: Why do some people have a better memory than others?
questions.english: Memory can differ because of attention, practice, familiarity and the conditions in which people learn. Someone who understands a subject well may connect new information more easily. Sleep and stress can also affect recall. I would not assume a strong memory is simply a fixed talent; useful strategies and repeated practice can improve how information is stored and retrieved.
questions.chinese: 记忆差异可能来自注意力、练习、熟悉程度和学习条件。理解某领域的人更容易连接新信息，睡眠和压力也影响回忆。我不会认为好记忆只是固定天赋；有效策略和反复练习能改善信息储存与提取。

questions.title: 想再去一次的城市
questions.text:
Describe a city that you have been to and would like to visit again
You should say:
When you visited it
What you did there
What it was like
And explain why you would like to visit it again
questions.english:
A city I have visited and would like to return to is Vienna, in Austria. I went there in June during a solo trip to Europe connected with an academic conference. I also visited Budapest, but spent more time in Vienna.

While I was there, I visited the Golden Hall and some local museums. Those places gave me a way to experience the city's cultural atmosphere. Its distinctive architecture is another reason it stands out as a destination, and the overall experience felt comfortable.

If I went again, I would like to spend more time appreciating the cultural places instead of only fitting them around the wider trip. I could read more about the exhibits beforehand and then explore at a slower pace. That would give a familiar city something new without requiring me to repeat exactly the same visit.

The reason I would choose Vienna is not that I have already seen everything. It is the opposite: the first visit gave me a starting point. A return trip would let me understand the places more deeply and enjoy the combination of museums, architecture and a comfortable atmosphere that makes the city appealing.
questions.chinese:
我去过、也想再访的城市是奥地利维也纳。今年六月，我独自赴欧洲参加学术会议，并在那趟旅行中去了那里，也去过布达佩斯，但在维也纳待得更久。

在那里，我参观金色大厅和一些当地博物馆，体验城市文化氛围。独特建筑也让它成为突出的目的地，整体体验很舒适。

如果再去，我想花更多时间欣赏文化场所，而不是只在整个行程的空当中安排参观。我可以提前多了解展品，再放慢探索节奏；这样熟悉城市也有新体验，不必完全重复上次。

选择维也纳，不是因为已经看遍一切，反而是首次访问给了起点。再去能更深入了解这些地方，享受博物馆、建筑和舒适氛围相结合的吸引力。
pending: 想再去维也纳及再访活动安排是候选愿望，未确认；不添加音乐会、具体博物馆或维也纳烤肉经历。

questions.title: 想再去一次的城市
questions.text: What should the government do to improve citizens' safety?
questions.english: Governments should make public spaces, transport and emergency services reliable. Good lighting, safer road design and clear reporting channels can prevent problems before they become serious. Enforcement should also be fair and consistent. I think safety depends on practical prevention and public trust, rather than only stricter punishment after harm has already occurred.
questions.chinese: 政府应保障公共空间、交通和应急服务可靠。良好照明、安全道路设计和清晰报告渠道，能在问题严重前预防它们。执法也应公平一致。我认为安全依赖实际预防和公众信任，而非只在伤害发生后加重惩罚。

questions.title: 想再去一次的城市
questions.text: Are there any changes in your city?
questions.english: I would expect some changes, particularly in transport, buildings and the services people use every day. A growing city may gain new facilities while familiar neighbourhoods also evolve. Not every change is automatically an improvement, though. I would judge it by whether daily life becomes more convenient and existing residents still feel included, rather than by the number of new buildings.
questions.chinese: 我想会有变化，尤其在交通、建筑和日常服务方面。发展的城市可能增加设施，熟悉的街区也会改变，但并非所有变化都自动变好。我会看生活是否更便利、原有居民是否仍被照顾，而非新建筑数量。
pending: 具体居住城市及已发生变化未提供；本稿未声称亲眼见到特定项目。

questions.title: 想再去一次的城市
questions.text: Do you think people in the countryside are friendlier than people in the city?
questions.english: People in the countryside may have more chances to know their neighbours, which can make interactions feel warmer. City residents may seem busy or distant when meeting strangers. However, that does not prove they are less kind. Friendliness depends on the person and the situation, so I would avoid turning a difference in familiarity into a judgement about character.
questions.chinese: 乡村居民可能更有机会认识邻居，让交流显得更热情。城市居民面对陌生人时可能忙碌或疏离，但这不证明他们更不善良。友好取决于个人和情境，因此不应把熟悉程度的差异变成性格判断。

questions.title: 想再去一次的城市
questions.text: Do you think it is possible that all of the population move to cities?
questions.english: I do not think everyone will move to cities. Cities offer jobs and services, but rural areas also have important roles, including food production and different lifestyles. Some people may prefer more space or closer ties to their community. Improving connections and services outside cities can give people genuine choices instead of making urban life the only workable option.
questions.chinese: 我认为不会人人都进城。城市有就业和服务，但乡村也承担粮食生产等重要作用，并提供不同生活方式。有些人更喜欢空间或社区联系。改善城外交通和服务，能给人真实选择，而非让城市生活成为唯一可行选项。

questions.title: 想再去一次的城市
questions.text: Some people say large cities are suitable for old people. What do you think?
questions.english: Large cities can suit older people because hospitals, shops and public transport may be easier to reach. However, noise, crowds and high costs can make life difficult. Accessibility matters more than size alone: safe crossings, lifts and nearby services can be essential. I would judge the particular neighbourhood and the person's needs rather than call every large city suitable.
questions.chinese: 大城市的医院、商店和公共交通可能更方便，适合老人，但噪声、拥挤和高成本也会带来困难。可及性比规模更重要，安全过街、电梯和近处服务可能很关键。我会看具体街区和个人需求，而非说所有大城市都合适。

questions.title: 想再去一次的城市
questions.text: What's the difference between the city and the countryside?
questions.english: Cities generally offer a wider range of jobs, services and entertainment, but they can also be crowded and expensive. The countryside may provide more space and a quieter environment, with fewer nearby facilities. Neither setting is automatically better. The choice depends on someone's work, family and priorities, and good transport can reduce some of the differences between them.
questions.chinese: 城市通常有更多工作、服务和娱乐，但也可能拥挤、昂贵。乡村空间更大、环境更安静，附近设施却可能较少。没有一方自动更好，选择取决于工作、家庭和优先事项，良好交通能缩小部分差异。

questions.title: 一见且想继续了解的人
questions.text:
Describe a person you only met once recently and want to know more about
You should say:
Who he/she is
When you met him/her
Why you want to know more about him/her
And explain how you feel about him/her
questions.english:
The person I'd like to describe is a man I chatted with while waiting for a train during my European trip in June. He was living on the streets, and the conversation was one small moment that stayed in my memory.

I only met him on that occasion. I cannot describe his background or explain how he came to be in that situation, because the conversation did not give me a complete account of his life. What I can say is that the interaction felt friendly, which contributed to my impression that people I encountered were welcoming.

I would like to know more about him as an individual rather than make assumptions based on his appearance or circumstances. For example, I would be interested in what he enjoys, which places matter to him and how he sees everyday life. Those questions are about the person, not just the label attached to him.

I feel that the meeting was a reminder to remain open to people outside my usual social circle. We did not need a long history together for the conversation to be meaningful. That is why he is someone I would be curious to meet again.
questions.chinese:
我想描述的人，是六月欧洲旅行中等火车时聊过的一名男子。他住在街头，这段谈话是旅行中一个留在我记忆里的小片段。

我只在那次遇见他，不能描述背景或解释他为何处于那种境遇，因为那次谈话并没有让我完整了解他的人生经历。可以说交流感觉友好，也让我觉得遇到的人很热情。

我想了解他这个具体的人，而不是根据外表或处境作假设，例如喜欢什么、哪些地方重要、怎么看日常生活。问题关乎本人，而非他身上的标签。

我觉得相遇提醒我，对平时社交圈之外的人保持开放。不需要多年交情，谈话也能有意义，所以我会想再次见到他。
pending: 只遇见一次、希望再了解的具体方向及引申感受为候选；男子身世、聊天城市与具体原话仍未知。

questions.title: 一见且想继续了解的人
questions.text: What should we not talk about when we meet a person for the first time?
questions.english: I would avoid intrusive questions about income, relationships or other private matters unless the person chooses to bring them up. Strong assumptions about their background can also make the conversation uncomfortable. It is usually easier to begin with the situation we share or a light interest. The aim is to create space for trust, not collect personal information immediately.
questions.chinese: 除非对方主动提起，我会避免问收入、感情等隐私，也避免强行假定对方背景。通常从共同情境或轻松兴趣开始更容易。目标应是给信任留空间，而不是马上收集私人信息。

questions.title: 一见且想继续了解的人
questions.text: What can we do to leave a good impression on people we meet for the first time?
questions.english: Being attentive, polite and genuinely interested is more useful than trying to impress someone with achievements. I would listen without interrupting, ask appropriate questions and remember the person's name if possible. A good first impression also comes from reliability, such as arriving on time. It should feel natural, because exaggerated praise or constant self-promotion can have the opposite effect.
questions.chinese: 专注、礼貌、真有兴趣，比用成就震住对方更有用。我会不打断地倾听、问合适问题，尽可能记住名字。准时等可靠行为也带来好印象。表现应自然，因为夸张赞美或不断自我推销可能适得其反。

questions.title: 一见且想继续了解的人
questions.text: What qualities make true friends?
questions.english: True friends are reliable, honest and willing to listen without making every conversation about themselves. They should respect boundaries and be able to disagree without humiliating each other. Support matters during difficulties, but sharing ordinary happiness is important too. I think friendship becomes stronger when both people contribute, rather than one person constantly providing all the attention and help.
questions.chinese: 真正朋友可靠、诚实、愿意倾听，不把所有谈话都变成自己的事。他们尊重边界，能不同意却不羞辱对方。困难时支持重要，分享日常快乐也重要。我认为双方都投入，友谊才更强，而不是一方始终付出全部关注和帮助。

questions.title: 一见且想继续了解的人
questions.text: Is it important to have the same hobbies and interests when making friends?
questions.english: Shared interests make it easier to start a conversation and arrange activities together. However, they are not essential for a strong friendship. Two people may enjoy different hobbies while still understanding each other's values and feelings. I would see common interests as a useful starting point, but trust, curiosity and respect are what allow the relationship to grow.
questions.chinese: 共同兴趣方便开启对话、安排活动，但不是牢固友谊的必要条件。两人爱好不同，仍可能理解彼此的价值观和感受。我把共同兴趣看作有用起点，而信任、好奇和尊重才让关系成长。

questions.title: 一见且想继续了解的人
questions.text: On what occasions do people like to make friends?
questions.english: People often make friends when they repeatedly meet in a setting that gives them something to discuss. School, work, clubs and shared projects are examples. Travel or a community event can also create an opportunity. The first meeting does not have to be dramatic; small conversations become a friendship when both people show interest and continue the contact.
questions.chinese: 人们在反复相遇、又有话可聊的环境中容易交朋友，比如学校、工作、社团和共同项目。旅行或社区活动也有机会。初次相遇不必惊天动地，双方有兴趣、持续联系时，小聊天就能发展为友谊。

questions.title: 一见且想继续了解的人
questions.text: How do people make friends in China?
questions.english: In China, people can meet friends through school, work, shared interests or introductions from existing friends. Online communities can also connect people, especially around specialised hobbies. The method is less important than what happens afterwards. A relationship usually develops through repeated conversations, shared experiences and reliability, rather than simply adding someone to a contact list.
questions.chinese: 在中国，人们通过学校、工作、共同兴趣或朋友介绍结识他人，网上社群也能连接人们，尤其是专门爱好。方法不如后续相处重要。关系通常靠反复交流、共同经历和可靠性发展，而非只把人加进通讯录。

questions.title: 送朋友的礼物
questions.text:
Describe a gift you would like to buy for your friend
You should say:
How you knew your friend
How long you have known him/her
How you would choose a gift for him/her
And explain why you would choose that gift for him/her
questions.english:
A gift I would like to buy for a friend is an illustrated book about the art and design behind Japanese animation. The friend I have in mind is a fellow student whom I first got to know during a conversation after a university seminar.

We have known each other for about two years. A shared interest in reading and animation gave us something easy to talk about at first, and the friendship developed through later conversations. That makes a book connected with those interests seem more personal than a random expensive present.

I would choose it by checking the sample pages, the quality of the illustrations and whether the language suits him. I would also try to find out discreetly whether he already owns it. The budget would be sensible, because I would not want the gift to create pressure to give something equally expensive back.

My reason for choosing it is that it offers more than an object to put on a shelf. He could enjoy the pictures, learn how a scene was created and return to it whenever he wanted. I think a gift is meaningful when it reflects attention to the person rather than simply the amount of money spent.
questions.chinese:
我想给朋友买一本介绍日本动漫背后艺术与设计的插图书。这位朋友是同学，我们在大学一次讲座后的交流中认识。

认识约两年。共同的阅读和动漫兴趣提供了最初的话题，之后通过更多交流发展友谊，因此，选择与这些兴趣相关的书，比随意买件昂贵的礼物更贴合这位朋友。

我会看样页、插图质量和语言是否适合，也会委婉确认他是否已有。预算会合理，因为不想让对方有同等昂贵回礼的压力。

我选择它，是因为这本书不只是一个摆在书架上的物件。他能欣赏图片、了解场景如何创作，随时重读。我认为有意义的礼物体现对人的关注，而非单纯花了多少钱。
pending: 朋友身份、约两年关系、共同兴趣及礼物计划为完整候选；未确认为用户真实朋友。

questions.title: 送朋友的礼物
questions.text: Are there any unlucky things that people should not buy as gifts in your country?
questions.english: Some gifts have cultural associations that people may consider unlucky. In China, a clock can be sensitive because the phrase for giving one sounds like a phrase connected with a funeral. However, beliefs vary between people and generations. I would consider the recipient's preferences rather than assume every cultural association is a strict rule for everyone.
questions.chinese: 有些礼物有可能被视为不吉利的文化联想。在中国，钟可能敏感，因为“送钟”的读音接近与葬礼有关的说法。但观念因人和代际而异。我会考虑收礼者偏好，而非假设所有文化联想都对人人构成严格禁忌。

questions.title: 送朋友的礼物
questions.text: What do people usually consider when buying gifts?
questions.english: People usually consider the recipient's interests, the occasion and their own budget. They may also ask whether the gift is useful, easy to keep and appropriate for the relationship. A thoughtful choice does not have to be expensive. I think knowing what someone actually enjoys is more valuable than buying something impressive simply because it has a famous label.
questions.chinese: 人们通常考虑收礼者兴趣、场合和预算，也会看礼物是否有用、好存放、适合这段关系。用心的礼物不必昂贵。我认为了解对方真正喜欢什么，比只因名牌而买看起来厉害的东西更有价值。

questions.title: 送朋友的礼物
questions.text: Which do people give on traditional festivals, red envelopes or other kinds of gifts?
questions.english: Both are used, depending on the festival and the relationship. Red envelopes are familiar during the Spring Festival, particularly as gifts for children, while food or other presents may suit different occasions. Money gives the recipient flexibility, but a chosen gift can feel personal. I would follow the family's preferences rather than insist that one form is always better.
questions.chinese: 两者都有，取决于节日和关系。春节红包很常见，尤其给孩子；其他场合可能更适合食品或别的礼物。钱让收礼者灵活使用，精心选的礼物则更个人化。我会尊重家庭偏好，不坚持一种永远更好。

questions.title: 送朋友的礼物
questions.text: Will people feel happy when receiving an expensive gift?
questions.english: An expensive gift may make someone happy if it suits them and feels sincerely given. But price alone cannot guarantee a positive reaction. They may feel uncomfortable, indebted or worried about returning the favour. I think the best gift shows understanding of the person, while staying appropriate for the relationship and the giver's budget.
questions.chinese: 贵礼物若合适且真诚，可能让人开心，但价格不保证积极反应。对方也可能不自在、觉得欠人情，或担心回礼。我认为好礼物体现对人的了解，同时适合关系、符合送礼者预算。

questions.title: 送朋友的礼物
questions.text: Is it hard to choose a gift?
questions.english: It can be difficult when we do not know the person's preferences or when the occasion feels important. There is also a risk of choosing something they already own. Asking discreetly or paying attention to their interests can help. I would rather choose a simple, suitable gift than spend too long searching for a supposedly perfect one.
questions.chinese: 不了解对方偏好、或场合很重要时，选礼物可能难，也可能买到已有的东西。适度询问、留意兴趣会有帮助。我更愿意选简单合适的礼物，而不是花太久寻找所谓完美礼物。

questions.title: 送朋友的礼物
questions.text: When do people normally send gifts to others?
questions.english: People often give gifts for birthdays, weddings, festivals or important milestones such as graduation. A gift can also express thanks or welcome someone without a formal celebration. The reason affects what is appropriate. I think it is useful to consider the relationship and the message being sent, rather than treat every occasion as requiring an expensive purchase.
questions.chinese: 人们常在生日、婚礼、节日或毕业等重要阶段送礼，也可在没有正式庆祝时表达感谢或欢迎。原因会影响合适的选择。我认为应考虑关系和想传达的信息，而非把每种场合都当成必须昂贵消费。

questions.title: 公共场所丢物品
questions.text:
Describe an occasion that you lost something in public
You should say:
What you lost
When and where you lost it
What you did to find it
And explain how you felt about it
questions.english:
An occasion when I lost something in public involved a pair of earphones. A few weeks ago, I was sitting in a café looking through some English notes on my laptop. When I left, I put the computer away but forgot the earphones on the table.

I noticed they were missing later, when I wanted to use them again. At first, I checked my bag several times, thinking I might have put them in the wrong pocket. Then I retraced the afternoon and remembered taking them out at the café.

I contacted the café and described the item and roughly where I had been sitting. A member of staff checked their lost property and told me that someone had handed in a pair matching the description. I went back and was able to collect them.

I felt embarrassed about the mistake, but also relieved and grateful. The useful lesson was not that I should blame myself for hours. It was that I needed a small routine before leaving a public place: check the table, check the seat and make sure the important items are actually in my bag.
questions.chinese:
一次在公共场所丢东西的经历，涉及一副耳机。几周前，我在咖啡馆用笔记本看英语笔记；离开时收好电脑，却把耳机落在桌上。

后来想用时才发现不见。最初多次查包，以为放错口袋，接着回想下午经过，记起在咖啡馆拿出来过。

我联系咖啡馆，描述物品和大致座位。工作人员检查失物，说有人交来相符的耳机。我回去取到了。

我为失误尴尬，也松口气、很感激。这件事给我的启示，不是让我长时间责怪自己，而是离开公共场所前需要养成一个简单的检查习惯：检查桌面、座位，确认重要物品已在包里。
pending: 耳机丢失、咖啡馆、发生时间、联系与取回全过程均为候选故事，未发生事实待确认。

questions.title: 公共场所丢物品
questions.text: What do people often feel after losing things?
questions.english: People may feel anxious, frustrated or embarrassed, particularly when the lost item is valuable or urgently needed. Losing something with personal memories can also be upsetting even if it costs little. The first reaction may make clear thinking difficult. Taking a moment to calm down and retrace the situation can help them decide what to do next.
questions.chinese: 人们可能焦虑、沮丧或尴尬，东西贵重或急需时尤其如此。带有个人回忆的物品即使不贵，丢了也会难过。最初反应可能影响清晰思考，先平静一下、回想经过，有助于决定下一步。

questions.title: 公共场所丢物品
questions.text: What can we do to reduce the possibility of losing things?
questions.english: Keeping important items in a consistent place is a simple way to reduce mistakes. Before leaving a train, café or classroom, people can check the items they brought. Carrying fewer loose objects also helps. Technology may assist with reminders or tracking, but a clear routine is still useful because a tool cannot prevent every moment of distraction.
questions.chinese: 把重要物品放在固定位置，是减少失误的简单方法。离开火车、咖啡馆或教室前，可以检查随身物品，少带零散物件也有帮助。技术能提醒或追踪，但清晰习惯仍有用，因为工具无法阻止每次分心。

questions.title: 公共场所丢物品
questions.text: What kinds of people may lose things often?
questions.english: People who are rushed, distracted or managing several tasks may be more likely to misplace things. An unfamiliar environment can also make it harder to follow a normal routine. I would not label someone careless simply because they lost an item once. The situation often matters, and a small change in habits can help more than blaming their personality.
questions.chinese: 匆忙、分心或同时处理多项任务的人可能更易弄丢东西。陌生环境也会打乱习惯。我不会因一次丢东西就认定某人粗心，情境常很重要，小幅调整习惯可能比责怪性格更有效。

questions.title: 公共场所丢物品
questions.text: Is it effective to offer rewards to find lost things?
questions.english: A reward may encourage someone to take extra time to return an item, especially when finding its owner is inconvenient. However, it is not a guarantee, and many people return things simply because it is the right action. Clear contact information and reporting the loss appropriately can matter too. I would treat a reward as an additional incentive, not the whole solution.
questions.chinese: 奖励可能鼓励人花更多时间归还物品，尤其寻找失主不方便时。但它不保证结果，很多人归还是因为这本来就对。清楚的联系方式和合适的挂失也重要。我会把奖励当额外激励，而非全部解决方案。

questions.title: 公共场所丢物品
questions.text: What will people do when losing things?
questions.english: People usually retrace their steps and check the places where they last used the item. They may ask staff, contact a lost-property office or notify someone who can help. If the item contains sensitive information, protecting that information is also important. A calm, organised search is usually more useful than repeatedly looking in the same place without a plan.
questions.chinese: 人们通常回走走过的路，检查最后用过物品的地方，也会问工作人员、联系失物处，或找能帮忙的人。若物品含敏感信息，也需保护信息。冷静、有条理地找，比没有计划地反复查同一处更有效。

questions.title: 公共场所丢物品
questions.text: What kinds of things do people usually lose?
questions.english: Small items that people carry and use frequently are easy to misplace, such as keys, phones, wallets or headphones. They may be put down briefly and forgotten when attention shifts. Documents or tickets can also be lost during travel. The pattern is often about movement and distraction, so having a designated place for essential items can reduce the risk.
questions.chinese: 经常携带使用的小物件容易放错，比如钥匙、手机、钱包或耳机。人们可能暂放后因注意转移而忘掉，旅途中也会丢文件或票。这往往与移动和分心有关，因此给重要物品固定位置能降低风险。

questions.title: 节约时间的方法/改变
questions.text:
Describe a way/change that helps you save a lot of time
You should say:
What it is
How you implement it
How difficult it is
And explain how you feel about the way/change
questions.english:
A change that helps me save a lot of time is using one consistent system for organising study files. Instead of leaving documents in different places with unclear names, I keep them in folders based on the subject and activity.

The way I implement it is fairly simple. I use a naming pattern, give each new file a meaningful title and keep the date when it helps distinguish versions. For something I revise, I preserve the earlier draft rather than create several confusing copies with almost identical names.

The most difficult part was the initial cleanup and remembering to follow the system. It is not technically advanced, but a routine only works when it is used consistently. I started with the materials I use most often instead of trying to reorganise every old document at once.

What I like is that the benefit appears repeatedly. Finding the right notes quickly and knowing which draft is current removes small interruptions throughout the day. It also makes reviewing easier. For me, the point is not to make folders look impressive, but to spend less attention searching and more attention actually learning.
questions.chinese:
一个帮我省许多时间的改变，是用统一系统整理学习文件。不再把命名不清的文件散放，而按科目和活动分类。

实施很简单：使用命名方式，给新文件有意义的标题，必要时保留日期以区分版本。修改材料时保存旧稿，避免出现几个名字几乎相同的混乱副本。

最难的是最初整理和记得遵循系统。技术不复杂，但这样的做法只有坚持使用才有效。我从最常用材料开始，没有一下整理全部旧文档。

我喜欢它的一点是，好处会反复体现出来：快速找到笔记、知道哪个是当前稿，减少一天里的小打断，也让复习更容易。目的不是让文件夹看起来厉害，而是少费心寻找，多专注学习。
pending: 整理系统、实际实施过程与个人省时效果为完整候选叙述，未确认用户已执行或已验证成效。

questions.title: 节约时间的方法/改变
questions.text: What can people do to save time?
questions.english: People can decide priorities, group similar tasks and reduce unnecessary interruptions. Preparing common items in advance also prevents repeated searching. However, saving time should not mean rushing every activity. Some tasks need patience and careful checking. I think the aim is to spend less time on avoidable friction so there is more time for the work and rest that matter.
questions.chinese: 人们可以确定优先级、集中处理相似任务、减少无谓打断。提前备好常用物品也省去反复寻找。但省时不意味着凡事赶，有些任务需要耐心和认真检查。目标应是减少可避免的阻碍，为重要工作和休息留时间。

questions.title: 节约时间的方法/改变
questions.text: Does technology help people save time? How and why?
questions.english: Technology can save time by automating routine steps, finding information quickly and helping people coordinate without travelling. For example, a shared document can reduce repeated messages. However, new tools also take time to learn, and notifications can interrupt concentration. The saving is real only when the tool solves a useful problem rather than creates extra work.
questions.chinese: 技术通过自动处理常规步骤、快速找信息、免出行协调来省时。例如，共享文档减少反复发消息。但新工具也需要学习时间，通知还会打断专注。只有工具解决有用问题、而非增加工作时，省时才真实。

questions.title: 节约时间的方法/改变
questions.text: Do you think parents should be responsible for teaching children to save time?
questions.english: Parents should help children learn basic time habits, but the responsibility can be shared with schools. Simple routines and realistic expectations work better than constant pressure to be productive. Parents can show how to prepare for an activity and allow enough time. Children also need play and rest, so managing time should include balance rather than eliminating every idle moment.
questions.chinese: 家长应帮助孩子学基本时间习惯，但学校也可分担。简单规律、现实要求，比持续逼孩子高效更好。家长能示范如何准备活动、留足时间。孩子也需要玩耍和休息，因此时间管理应包含平衡，而非消灭所有空闲。

questions.title: 节约时间的方法/改变
questions.text: Do people who can manage time well become successful more easily?
questions.english: Good time management can help people make consistent progress and meet commitments, so it may improve their chances of success. But it is not the only factor. Skills, resources, opportunities and unexpected events also matter. Someone can organise time well and still face serious obstacles, so I would not judge success or failure solely by a person's schedule.
questions.chinese: 良好时间管理帮助持续进步、履行承诺，因此可能增加成功机会，但并非唯一因素。技能、资源、机会和意外事件也重要。安排得好仍可能遇到严重障碍，所以我不会只凭日程判断成功或失败。

questions.title: 节约时间的方法/改变
questions.text: Is it necessary for children to learn time management?
questions.english: Yes, children benefit from learning to prepare, estimate how long a task takes and remember commitments. These skills can make daily life less stressful. The teaching should match their age and leave room for mistakes. I would not expect a young child to follow an adult's strict timetable, because learning independence takes practice and support.
questions.chinese: 需要。孩子学会准备、估计任务时长、记住承诺，能降低日常压力。教学应符合年龄，允许犯错。我不会要求小孩子遵守成人的严格时间表，因为独立需要练习和支持。

questions.title: 节约时间的方法/改变
questions.text: What can schools do to help students learn time management?
questions.english: Schools can divide larger assignments into stages and show students how to plan each step. Calendars, short checklists and reflection on missed deadlines can be useful. Teachers should also coordinate workload so expectations are realistic. The aim is not simply to punish lateness, but to help students recognise priorities and make a plan they can actually follow.
questions.chinese: 学校可以把大作业分阶段，示范如何规划每一步。日历、简短清单和对错过截止日期的反思都能帮助。老师也应协调工作量，让要求现实。目标不只是罚迟交，而是帮助识别优先级，做出真正能执行的计划。
